### [17] [Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27326)
*Rabimba Karanjai,Suryabhan Singh Hada,Hemanth Hegadehalli Madhavarao,Qun Gu,Libin N. George,Wenhuan Sun,Neha Monga,Richard Williamson,Prakhar Mehrotra*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出一种**无损**的中间推理压缩框架：在推理语料上用 BPE 学习高频语义片段，并为其分配私有使用区（PUA）Unicode 码点作为"概念词元"，扩展 LLM 词表后经由 Fast Vocabulary Transfer 初始化嵌入 + 自蒸馏 LoRA 微调，使模型直接在压缩空间中推理。编码严格 1:1，压缩轨迹可完全还原为可读文本。在 Llama-3.1-8B、Qwen2.5-14B/32B 与 GSM8K、MATH、StrategyQA、CommonsenseQA 上，总生成词元平均减少 14.7%（推理链最长减少 27.1%），准确率平均仅下降 1.6 个百分点，且该方法与已有有损压缩正交、可叠加使用。

（注：标题与相关工作/第 3 节强调"多语言 scratchpad"与"中英跨语言推理"，但最终方法与实验实际只在英文语料上开展，中文仅作为基线对照与 CTR 分析素材；摘要段落存在被截断的表述。）


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 链式思维（CoT）提示能显著提升 LLM 在数学、逻辑、常识推理上的能力，但自回归解码使长推理链的延迟与成本近似线性增长，给大规模部署带来严重算力瓶颈。现有降本路线均有明显代价：连续潜空间内部化（Coconut、pause token、隐状态计算）与生成期跳词/剪枝（TokenSkip 等）不可逆地摧毁推理轨迹的可读性，牺牲可解释性与可审计性；而"改用中文或"请简洁"式提示虽能省词元，却并非真正的 1:1 压缩——它会不可预测地改变生成策略，静默省略验证步骤或逻辑环节（作者用固定内容分析证明）。因此核心问题是：如何系统性减少中间推理中被处理的词元数量，同时不改变逻辑步骤、也不牺牲人类可读性与可审计性？作者认为语言之间的表示效率差异是真实存在的（如同一文本跨语言 token 数可差 15 倍），但必须对具体 tokenizer 与具体 checkpoint 直接实测，而不能想当然地假设中文更省。

Method: **（1）压缩语言构建（Stage 1）**：用基础 tokenizer 切分训练语料 D_o，迭代统计相邻符号对频次，将最高频对全局合并为新符号 ṽ_t，直至最高频次低于阈值 τ=5（或达到合并预算 K）；每个新符号分配一个 PUA 码点（U+E000–U+F8FF），因此 V_c 与原文空间不冲突、渲染与还原均为单 token。得到严格 1:1 的编码映射 Enc: V_o*→V* 与其逆 Dec: V*→V_o*，压缩语料 D_c = Enc(D_o)。数字、数学符号、LaTeX 符号被排除在合并之外，保留为普通 token，以避免模型需大量训练才能掌握符号化 PUA 表示。

**（2）词表扩展与嵌入热启动（Stage 2）**：V = V_o ∪ V_c，新 token 的输入/输出嵌入 E_c、W_c 用 Fast Vocabulary Transfer 初始化为其构成原始 token 嵌入的均值；随后仅解冻 E_c、W_c（其余全冻结）在 D_c 上做 2 epoch 因果语言建模损失微调（3×H100）。

**（3）压缩空间自蒸馏微调（Stage 3）**：冻结原模型生成原始语言 CoT c ~ M_θ(·|q)，对 query 与每步推理同时施加 Enc 得到 (q^c, c^c)，构成自蒸馏集 S^c；在冻结 θ 上仅训练 LoRA 适配器 φ（3–4 epoch，3×H100），目标是让模型"在输入所处的表示空间中推理"，而非教授新的推理能力。

**（4）度量方法论**：提出 **概念归一化词元率 CTR(m,ℓ,z) = |τ_m(r_ℓ(z))| / K**，其中 z 为固定 K 个带类型语义原子（声明、操作、关系、答案断言）构成的规范轨迹，r_ℓ 为确定性渲染器；因轨迹内容固定，CTR 降低不可能来自省略推理，从而把"表示效率"与"生成策略变化"解耦，并按语言与 tokenizer 双重索引。

**（5）实验设置**：三个 checkpoint（Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct、Qwen2.5-14B/32B-Instruct）× 四个数据集（GSM8K、MATH、StrategyQA、CommonsenseQA）；以各模型自身 tokenizer 为基础，仅英文语料训练 codec；CommonsenseQA 无 CoT 故仅作原始臂评测（作为分布外泛化测试）。由于 vLLM 批量服务下墙钟延迟不可比，统一以生成/提示词元数作为效率指标。

Result: **压缩强度**：语料层面词元减少 10.3%–18.7%（GSM8K 最高，StrategyQA 最低）；仅新增 2,944（LLaMA）/2,919（Qwen）个概念 token 于十万级基础词表之上，MATH 单独即触发约 95% 的 codec。

**端到端效果（12 个模型×数据集组合）**：总生成词元平均减少 **14.7%**（区间 5.6%–20.4%）；在"raw 与 compressed 同时答对"的匹配子集上，**纯推理链长度下降 4.9%–27.1%（均值约 18%）**，说明收益主要来自更短的推理而非更短的提示。准确率平均变动 **−1.6 个百分点**，5/12 行下降不足 1 点，最差为 Llama-8B 在 GSM8K 的 82.3%→78.6%（−3.7），另有 3 行持平或反超（Llama-8B MATH 38.0%→39.4%；Qwen-32B StrategyQA 81.2%→81.9%；Qwen-14B StrategyQA 持平）。

**真实使用压缩空间**：压缩臂生成词元中 PUA 占比 11.2%–26.1%（raw 臂恒为 0），证明模型确在概念词表内推理而非仅压缩输入。

**模型差异**：Qwen2.5-14B/32B 全面平顺适配（近乎零精度代价）；Llama-3.1-8B 泛化最差（GSM8K −3.7、CommonsenseQA −3.6，且 CommonsenseQA 仅省 5.6%），与作者"基线单语能力 + 模型容量决定采纳新表示空间能力"的判断一致。

**方法论与兼容性结论**：CTR 分析表明"用中文/简洁英文省钱"主要靠改变生成策略（省略步骤），并非 1:1 表示压缩；本方法把"序列紧凑性"与"推理精确性"彻底解耦，因 Enc/Dec 互逆，推理完全可审计、可还原，并可与 TokenSkip 等有损方法叠加。

**局限**：prompt 与答案仅限英文，多语言整体体验未验证；CTR 依赖单一确定性渲染器，缺少母语者改写与语言合规性追踪；仅以完成词元数作为解码代价代理，未纳入延迟、显存、KV-cache、能耗；路由器依赖单一数据划分与确定性解码，缺少阈值锁定与重复评估。

Conclusion: 本文证明：中间推理可以通过**形式化构造的无损压缩表示**（BPE 学习的高频语义片段 + PUA 概念词元 + FVT 嵌入热启动 + 自蒸馏 LoRA）系统性缩短，而非依赖"换个语言/写短些"这类会改变生成策略的启发式做法。在不牺牲可读性与可审计性的前提下，平均节省 14.7% 生成词元、推理链最多缩短 27.1%，精度代价约 1.6 个百分点，且与已有有损压缩方法正交、可叠加。作者由此主张"紧凑性不必以可解释性为代价"，并指出未来通过扩大语料规模与合并预算 K 可回收更多冗余、以获得更高信息密度的推理中间层；同时承认需补充硬件级效率指标与真正的多语言端到端评测。

Abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) but incurs high inference costs due to lengthy autoregressive decoding. While previous efficiency approaches reduce costs by discarding tokens or utilizing continuous latent representations, these lossy methods fundamentally sacrifice interpretability and auditability. In this work, we introduce a novel compression framework for intermediate reasoning. We apply Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) to reasoning corpora to learn a compressed vocabulary of Private Use Area (PUA) tokens, each representing frequent semantic spans. After expanding the LLM's vocabulary, we fine-tune the model via strictly 1:1, our method is lossless. We evaluate our approach on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B, and Qwen2.5-32B across four diverse benchmarks. Our method reduces total generated tokens by 14.7% on average with reasoning trace lengths dropping by up to 27.1%, while incurring a negligible average accuracy cost of 1.6 percentage points. Crucially, this approach is orthogonal to existing lossy methods, allowing practitioners to stack lossless and irreversible compression techniques. We demonstrate that a compressed intermediate language provides a highly efficient computational resource that accelerates inference while fully preserving the transparency of LLM reasoning.

</details>


### [18] [WaXup: Weight Averaging of Experts as Data Augmentation for Robust Introspection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27353)
*Marc Boëlle,Lucas Dixon,Alexandre Ramé*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 提出 WaXup：借鉴计算机视觉中的 MiXup，将“权重空间线性插值”作为一种数据增强手段来训练大模型的“可训练内省器”（introspector），使其能以自然语言准确描述自身微调获得的行为/任务，并显著提升其在权重空间分布偏移（如 LoRA 秩、学习率、训练轮数变化、对抗性隐藏行为）下的鲁棒性与泛化性，且无需额外微调任何专家模型。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 传统机制可解释性方法（人工检查权重/激活、稀疏自编码器等）难以跟上 LLM 能力与规模的增长，难以扩展。一种新范式是“可训练内省”（trainable introspection）：把模型自身当作诊断工具，训练一个可插拔的内省适配器（如 LoRA 模块 τ），使其根据与预训练检查点的权重差异推断并用自然语言描述该模型被微调的任务/隐藏行为。已有工作（Goel et al. 2026；Shenoy et al. 2026）表明在“微调专家数据集”上做 SFT 可得到初步可用的内省器，但存在两大瓶颈：(1) 可用的微调专家数量有限（每个专家都需要额外微调成本），扩展性差；(2) 内省器脆弱——极易记忆训练集中的专家权重（300 步内训练损失降至 1e-2 以下），在输入模型分布发生偏移（协变量偏移，如不同 LoRA 秩、学习率、训练步数、损失函数，甚至对抗性隐藏行为）时性能显著退化。而“训练一次、审计多个”（train-once, audit-many）的实用审计范式要求内省器对未知微调具备强泛化能力，因此亟需低成本地扩充并多样化训练集中的模型数量与多样性。

Method: **核心思想**：把视觉领域的 MiXup（对输入与标签做线性插值产生“合成”样本）类比迁移到模型权重空间——依据线性模式连通性（linear mode connectivity）性质，从同一预训练检查点微调出的专家位于权重空间中相连区域，权重插值得到的模型其行为介于两个专家之间。

**形式化**：设数据集 D={(θ_i, x_i, y_i)}，θ_i 为从同一基座微调的专家权重，x_i 为自然语言内省提问，y_i 为任务/行为描述。目标是学习单个内省器 τ（LoRA），使 θ_i⊕τ 能回答 x_i 并生成 y_i，损失为长度归一化自回归交叉熵 L_SFT。协变量偏移被重新解释为：内省器 f_τ: θ → p_{θ⊕τ} 的输入权重来自权重空间中不同的分布。

**WaXup 增强**：以概率 p_mix 对小批量中的样本，随机配对另一专家 (θ'_i, y'_i)，采样 λ∼Beta(α,α)（对称分布），构造插值模型 θ̃ = λ·θ_i ⊕ (1−λ)·θ'_i，再对 θ̃⊕τ 计算混合目标 L̃：
1) *加权目标*：L̃ = λ·L_SFT(θ̃⊕τ, x_i, y_i) + (1−λ)·L_SFT(θ̃⊕τ, x_i, y'_i)（无需任何额外预处理）；
2) *合并目标*：用 LLM 将两段描述改写为单一合并描述 ỹ，再对 ỹ 做标准 SFT 损失（适合复杂行为）。
当目标为单 token 时，加权目标可写为标准 MiXup 的软标签交叉熵（附录 A 给出等价性证明）。

**实现**：使用 Kauldron 库的批量多任务 LoRA 训练，权重平均在设备端直接对稠密更新 ΔW=B·A 做插值，不物化稠密矩阵到 CPU；加权目标通过复制 batch（每个插值模型分别配两个目标）实现。

**实验设置**：三个基准——(a) Goel et al. 的 hidden-behavior 基准（Gemma 3 1B，4760 个 rank-1 LoRA “主题粉丝”专家，训练 4660 个，测试 100 个留出主题，并按 LoRA 秩 1–64 做分布偏移）；(b) Super-Natural Instructions 派生的真实 NLP 任务元数据集（987 个任务，897 训练模型 + 90 测试模型，Gemma 3 1B/4B）；(c) AuditBench（56 个对抗训练隐藏行为模型 + 520 个 Qwen3-14B 专家训练集，衡量 verbalization rate）。评测用 LLM-judge 1–5 分，并做双评审一致性、人工一致性及嵌入相似度（gemini-embedding-2）三重稳健性验证。消融对比：高斯噪声注入、随机缩放（λ~U([0.7,1.3])）。

Result: 1) **隐藏行为基准**：WaXup 在全部测试秩上优于基线；同秩（rank-1）时提升较小（4.73→4.76），偏移越大提升越明显（如 rank-64：4.62→4.67~4.70）。
2) **NLP 任务基准**：Gemma 3 1B 基线平均 4.63–4.64，WaXup 提升至 4.81–4.89；Gemma 3 4B 基线 4.30–4.42，WaXup 提升至 4.61–4.75，且对训练/测试秩的四种组合全部占优（表 1）。训练损失/验证损失曲线显示 WaXup 保持较高训练损失却有更低验证损失（缓解过拟合）。
3) **其他协变量偏移**（学习率、训练轮数、秩+学习率/轮数的组合）：WaXup 的泛化曲线随训练模型数增加更陡，偏移带来的性能衰减更小。
4) **AuditBench**：基线约 300 步即达峰后开始退化（因已记忆训练模型）；WaXup 训练全程持续提升，75% 合并模型比例下 verbalization rate 相对基线峰值提升 +4.7pp（相对 +31%）。分配置看：transcript+KTO +7.3pp(+44%)、transcript+SFT +5.1pp(+28%)、合成文档+SFT +3.7pp(+19%)；合成文档+KTO（最难）仅 +0.36pp(+4.4%)，作者归因于该设置距训练分布过远、基线本身几乎不优于“无内省器”设置。合并比例从 25%→75% 持续提升并降低种子间方差。
5) **消融**：高斯噪声注入基本中性甚至略负（4.50–4.67，低于基线）；随机缩放略优于基线（4.68–4.80）但无法匹配 WaXup，说明收益不仅来自输入多样性，更来自专家间的线性几何结构。
6) **评测可靠性**：双 LLM 评审一致性高（隐藏行为 exact 90.7%、κw=0.86；NLP 94.4%、κw=0.93；AuditBench raw 95.7%、κ=0.84），人工与 LLM 评审一致性 96–97%（AuditBench 89%），嵌入相似度指标结论一致。

Conclusion: WaXup 提供了一个简单、低开销、无需额外微调专家模型的数据增强框架，通过在权重空间做线性插值并配合两种文本空间混合目标（加权 SFT 损失或 LLM 合并描述），有效扩充内省器训练集的多样性，抑制对训练专家的记忆，显著提升内省器在分布偏移与对抗性隐藏行为上的鲁棒性与泛化性，同时在部分场景提升数据效率。局限与展望：线性插值只能重组已有专家，无法创造未见任务/行为，故必须与扩大/多样化初始专家池互补；合并模型的监督信号（描述生成）仍有改进空间；内省器绑定于特定基座架构与检查点；更大的后训练目标变化（如从 SFT 到 RL）与更广行为偏移仍是挑战；架构上可引入对权重差异的显式链式推理，以及与 LoRAcles 等权重空间方法或 DPO 阶段结合。作者认为鲁棒的内省器对于未来 LLM 自主读写权重、自我改进场景下的“可监控性”具有重要意义。

Abstract: As the capabilities of large language models keep improving, traditional mechanistic interpretability methods struggle to keep pace. In contrast, trainable introspection methods emerge as a promising alternative; they repurpose the model itself as a self-diagnostic tool, trained to verbalize what it has learned during finetuning in natural language. While training on datasets of finetuned experts achieves encouraging results, it currently lacks robustness and generalization. Building on the data augmentation framework of MiXup, we introduce WaXup, a method that augments the introspection training set through linear interpolation in the weight space. This is motivated by the linear mode connectivity property: weight averaged experts interpolate the behaviors of the initial experts. We evaluate WaXup on three benchmarks: hidden-behavior models, a meta-dataset of real-world NLP tasks and AuditBench, a challenging alignment auditing suite of models adversarially trained to conceal their behaviors. WaXup improves the accuracy of generated descriptions as well as robustness to various distribution shifts. We hope to improve the reliability of trainable introspection methods towards better and safer models.

</details>


### [19] [No Audio, No Transcripts, No Problem: LLM-based ASR Adaptation Using Only Domain Documents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27434)
*Sergio Burdisso,Dairazalia Sánchez-Cortés,Esaú Villatoro-Tello,Thibault Bañeras-Roux,Manjunath K E,Kadri Hacioglu,Petr Motlicek,Andreas Stolcke*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文首次研究"仅用目标域文档（无音频、无转写）"的 LLM-based ASR 域适配：把文档原句直接作为适配文本，或用 LLM 零样本将文档改写成合成口语对话，再送入已有的多视图去噪 text-only 适配方法。实验表明，仅文档适配可匹配甚至超过使用真实转写的效果；哪种渲染更优取决于目标语音语体（form）与生成文本量（quantity）。同时作者构建并发布了文档配准基准。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: LLM-based ASR（语音编码器 + 冻结 LLM + 轻量投影器）在域偏移下性能下降，转写目标域音频做适配又昂贵，因此 text-only 适配（仅用文本）成为有吸引力的替代方案。然而既有所有 text-only 适配工作（中间 CTC、语言模型融合、文本到频谱、Whisper 解码器适配、投影器坍塌监测、软提示、以及多视图去噪方法）都建立在一个几乎未加检验的假设上：目标域文本是真实口语对话的 ground-truth 转写。而最现实的新客户上线场景恰恰相反——客户只提供原始文档（官网、产品说明、手册、政策等），域内通话转写恰恰是不可得的；获取转写就等于要重新做语音采集与标注，与 text-only 适配的初衷相悖。此外，从已有文档适配符合隐私友好部署：无需录制和转写敏感客户对话。因此核心问题是：能否只用原始文档、既无目标域音频也无目标域转写，就把 ASR 适配到新域？作者进一步指出文档与转写的差异不仅在内容（content），更在形式（form）：文档是书面散文，转写是自发、含不流畅、轮次化的话语——这是本文的方法学出发点。

Method: 问题设定：源域有配对音频-转写集 D_src 用于训练基座模型；目标域仅有原始文档集合 C_tgt（无音频、无转写）。

（1）文档→适配文本的两种渲染。Written：直接把文档切分为句子作为目标文本。Conversational：用指令微调 LLM（Gemma 4:31B，SDialog 工具包，Markdown 输入以利用标题与列表，采样温度 2.0）零样本地把每篇文档渲染为一通 Agent–Customer 电话对话；提示词强制四项属性：文档接地（事实仅来自文档、沿用术语、不新增事实）、轮次式短语音单元切分（不规则非交替说话人、独立 backchannel）、自发口语风格（重启、重复、犹豫、填充词等不流畅性）、ASR 式文本规范化（数字/日期/邮箱拼读，USA/FBI 逐字母拼读、其他缩写展开，全大写无标点）。每次生成独立均匀采样一篇文档，生成对话数 N 与文档数 M 解耦；输出单个 JSON 的 {speaker, text} 列表，每个 text 段作为一条转写。

（2）适配骨干：采用已有的多视图去噪 text-only 适配方法，将 LLM-based ASR 视为去噪任务——投影器 sp(·) 输出的软 token 被视为转写的"含噪文本渲染"，LLM 学习将其"清洗"回文本。每个 mini-batch 由四个视图按比例混合：σ_a（源域音频-文本对）、σ_ta（投影器诱导的近邻词表噪声 noise_a(t)）、σ_t（合成噪声源转写）、τ（合成噪声的目标域转写，驱动适配）；本文固定 τ=0.5（σ_a=σ_ta=σ_t≈0.17），其余骨干超参数不变，使"文本来源"成为唯一变量。训练提示词为 "Transcribe speech to text. Speech: {input}"。

（3）系统配置：SLAM-ASR 框架，WavLM-Large 编码器 + Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct 解码器，单隐层（ReLU + 回归层）投影器；基座仅训投影器 5 epoch（lr 1e-4、1000 warm-up、batch 10）；适配用 LoRA（仅 self-attention 的 query/value，rank 16、α=32）微调 LLM，5 epoch、lr 1e-4、1000 warm-up。

（4）文档配准基准构建（因无公开语料同时具备音频+转写+文档，且 DefinedAI 使用虚构产品名无法爬网）：仅用每个域的训练集转写合成文档，且生成只接收抽象化信号——步骤为话题发现（BERTopic 式 class-based TF-IDF，Optuna 100 trials 调参最大化 c_v 一致性，涵盖 LSA/NMF/UMAP 与 KMeans/HDBSCAN）、话题标注（LLM）、实体/关键词抽取（LLM，实体、领域术语、事实性短语）、文档生成（LLM 写结构化 Markdown，≤9000 词，打乱实体列表增加多样性）；生成后校验至少 90% 抽取到的实体与关键词出现，否则重生成。此构建仅用于建基准，适配流程从不接触目标域转写。

（5）语料与条件：DefinedAI（专有客服电话语料；源域 Banking+Insurance+Healthcare，目标为不相交子集的 B/I/H 及未见的 Telco、Retail）与 SlideSpeech（公开的演示/讲座语料；源域 Life/Talent/English，目标 Agriculture/Animation/Musical Instruments，全为未见域）。四种条件：Base、Transcripts（真实转写上界）、Written、Conversational，指标为 WER 与相对 Base 的改善 Δ。另设开发域 Banking 的 few-shot 提示分析与一次性设计的固定提示词说明。

Result: DefinedAI（会话语体）：Conversational 几乎完全追平真实转写——与 Transcripts 的绝对 WER 差最大仅 0.28（Banking 9.41 vs 9.13），Retail 上甚至优于转写（17.18 vs 17.59，Δ=16.1%）；而 Written 明显偏弱，在 Healthcare 上比 Base 更差（7.63 vs 6.85，Δ=-11.4%），Banking/Insurance 也仅接近或略优于 Base。原因在于文档虽按构造含实体与关键词，但书面形式缺乏 ASR 需建模的口语特征。

SlideSpeech（演示/讲座语体）：真实转写本身收益很小（Δ≤7.1%），headroom 有限；此时 Written 反而有竞争力（Agriculture 16.09 vs 转写 16.01），因文档的说明性句子已契合演示语体，而面向客服对话的提示词拟合较差；且默认设置受数据量限制（r_c≈0.06，仅 51–141 段对话），将 Agriculture/Animation 扩到 1000 段对话（40k/31k 语音段）后 WER 从 16.27/16.13 降至 16.17/15.68，接近真实转写（16.01/15.55），Animation 提升更明显。

跨域（DefinedAI→SlideSpeech，最难）：Base WER 高达 47–59，三种文本来源都大致把 WER 减半且彼此接近；Conversational 相对 Base 改善 44.9/43.2/39.9%，Written 改善 44.1/38.0/45.3%，真实转写改善 49.5/39.6/45.2%；Animation 上 Conversational 超过真实转写（27.36 vs 29.12），Musical Instruments 上 Written 与真实转写几乎相同（25.73 vs 25.76）。此处即使使用默认的小生成量也能回收大部分收益，说明当基座距目标域很远时，headroom 极大，少量域内文本即足够——这是支持"新客户上线"设想的最强证据。

Few-shot：Banking 上 0/1/3/10-shot 的平均 WER 为 9.41/9.23/9.21/9.42，均在转写上界 9.13 的 0.3 以内，3-shot 最好但仅 0.1 优势，10-shot 反而最不稳定；因任何 few-shot 都需要真实域内转写（违背 document-only 前提），全文采用零样本生成。提示词仅在开发域 Banking 上设计一次后冻结，未按域调优，故结果偏保守。

Conclusion: 仅用目标域原始文档（无音频、无转写）适配 LLM-based ASR 是可行且有前景的新范式：把文档原句直接用作适配文本，或由 LLM 零样本渲染为合成口语对话，再经去噪式 text-only 适配，Conversational 渲染通常能接近、有时匹配甚至超过真实转写适配；Written 渲染在目标语体与文档书面语体吻合（如演示式语料）或基座模型距目标域很远时具竞争力，但在会话式语料上可能明显不足、甚至损害 Base 性能。作者归纳出决定性因素：内容由构造固定，形式（form）对会话语音起决定作用，数量（quantity）在形式合适但文本池偏小时接替成为主导，而在跨域大 headroom 情形下二者均不构成瓶颈。意义在于使 ASR 适配可基于客户已拥有的文档完成，无需录制或转写敏感通话，契合隐私友好部署。局限与未来工作：提示词未针对各域优化、基准文档由训练转写抽象合成、跨语体生成提示尚需调整；作者发布 SlideSpeech 的合成文档与对话及全部代码以支持后续研究。

Abstract: Can a speech recognizer be adapted to a new domain with no target audio and no transcripts, using only written documentation? This is the realistic onboarding setting: a new customer hands over raw documentation, not the transcripts that text-only adaptation normally assumes. We turn a domain's documents into adaptation text in two ways, directly as written sentences or rendered by a large language model (LLM) into synthetic spoken dialogs, and feed them to a recently proposed denoising-based text-only adaptation method. We show that, across in-domain, out-of-domain, and cross-domain settings on two corpora, document-only adaptation can match or closely approach real transcriptions; whether written or conversational rendering is best depends on speaking style and the amount of text generated. To our knowledge, this is the first study of document-only adaptation of LLM-based ASR. As no existing corpus pairs audio, transcripts, and documents, we also built and released a document-grounded benchmark.

</details>


### [20] [Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27491)
*Jonathan von Rad,Pontus Stenetorp,Yao Lu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文通过受控预训练实验（39个1B decoder-only模型、5种语言、4种分词器）发现：改进词表分配会显著提升模型早-中层（第0-8层）的跨语言表示对齐，并增强FFN神经元中的跨语言参数化事实知识共享（相关+因果证据），但**不改变**跨语言迁移（BTS）表现，形成"对齐-迁移解离"；同时在公平词表分配下跨文字（cross-script）语言对的迁移与共享仍显著更低，说明"文字屏障"并非分词器伪影。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 多语言分词器常将词表过度分配给高资源语言，使低资源语言切分效率下降、性能受损。已有研究主要关注分词对性能/效率的影响，对其如何塑造预训练过程中的跨语言表示对齐（alignment）与迁移（transfer）缺乏系统理解；且先前仅在输出层测量对齐的工作（如Limisiewicz等报告词表分配对句子检索无影响）可能掩盖了中间层效应。此外，"更强的对齐是否真的带来更好的迁移"在学界仍有争议（Hua等指出对齐可无迁移地出现，Gaschi等报告正相关）。作者希望隔离"词表分配"这一唯一变量，检验分词是否是此前迁移/文字屏障结论的伪影。

Method: 1) 实验设计：预训练39个LLaMA风格decoder-only模型（1.09B参数，16层，hidden 2048，FFN 5632 SwiGLU，16头，RMSNorm，RoPE，untied embeddings），语料为FineWeb2-HQ（英语用FineWeb-HQ），共7个分词器条件：starved（复现Longpre等的419语言分词器，Unigram，T=100）、20语言、fair（5语言，byte-premium调整采样）、以及4个按语言对定制的2语言分词器；全部固定64k词表、SentencePiece Unigram；最多30B tokens，AdamW/bf16，WSD（1B预热/23B稳定/6B衰减），batch 1M tokens；算力4330 GH200 GPU-h + 2930 Chip-h。2) 评估：①对齐——用MEXA在FLORES+上逐层计算平行句双向检索准确率μ_{s,t}(l)；②迁移——以BPB计的目标语言验证损失差异定义BTS^loss_{s→t}（对比等目标语言暴露下的单语/双语模型，仅在WSD稳定阶段1–24B），并辅以下游准确率BTS^perf；③参数化知识共享——对PolyFact上双语均答对的事实用integrated gradients定位FFN知识神经元，计算跨语言Jaccard重叠及因果消融迁移率CTR=(d_cross−b_cross)/(d_own−b_own)（用不同事实基线控制）；④logit lens分析事实可解码层深度。4) 控制变量分析：在80个稳定阶段检查点上拟合线性模型，同时控制log分配与质量指标（训练token数、BPB、BPB²、伙伴语言事实准确率），以配对bootstrap给出95% CI。

Result: (1) 表征对齐：更少语言训练的"公平/饥饿程度低"分词器显著提高第0–8层对齐（2–5B tokens即出现，持续至30B）；en-de首次达到MEXA≥0.90的层从第13层前移到10–12层，说明只看输出层会漏掉效应；对齐随分配量总体上升但非严格单调（法语在20→5语言间变化小，中文在5→2语言间下降，可能因多字token边际收益递减）。(2) logit lens显示公平分词器下正确事实在更浅层即可解码（约提前0.2–2层），解释了早期中层对齐的来源。(3) 跨语言迁移：四种分词器下的BTS排序（法语受益最大、德语近中性、阿语与中文负迁移）完全一致，迁移入伙伴语言的分词器效应均在0.5个百分点内，仅"20语言→英语"一项CI排除零（F(3,9)=1.05, p=0.42；迁移入英语 F=3.33, p=0.07），即分词器对迁移影响边际——形成"对齐-迁移解离"；同文字对（en-de/en-fr）迁移与共享始终高于跨文字对（en-ar/en-zh），表明文字屏障不是分词器伪影。(4) 参数化知识共享：对源语言top-100知识神经元做因果消融显著降低目标语言事实对数似然（超过不同事实基线3–7 nats，随机神经元消融≤0.02 nats），提供因果证据；CTR随分配量上升（法语0.34→0.56，阿语0.10→0.33），中文几乎无改善；神经重叠（Jaccard）在K∈{50,100,200,500}下结论稳健，且在匹配事实召回率（±1pp）的检查点上仍成立。(5) 质量控制：控制训练token数/BPB/BPB²/事实准确率后，对齐效应仍保留约3/4（β=0.33→0.24–0.26），共享效应保留约一半到三分之二（重叠0.028→0.016–0.020；CTR 0.116→0.055–0.077），即模型质量只能解释部分增益。(6) 其他：更公平分词使模型在相同token预算下多读20–48%文本，下游基准总体提升（BMLAMA平均+7pp，德语+5.2，英语+2.3）；英语是"强供体、弱受体"，迁移入英语普遍为负且随训练更负。

Conclusion: 核心结论有三：(1) 改进词表分配带来两个新效应——早-中层跨语言表示对齐大幅提高（并伴随"更早承诺输出"的深度效应），以及FFN神经元中跨语言参数化事实知识共享增强（相关与因果双重证据），提示更公平的分配可能是缓解多语言"参数竞争诅咒"的杠杆；(2) 尽管对齐与共享显著改善，改进分词**并未**提升跨语言迁移，构成对齐-迁移解离，说明表征相似性/知识共置并不自动转化为迁移收益，语言对特性比分词质量更重要；(3) 在公平词表分配下跨文字语言对的迁移与共享差距依然存在，故"文字屏障"是真实的、超越分词器伪影的现象。作者呼吁未来跨语言交互研究采用更公平（词表均衡）的实验设置。局限：每种文字类别仅2个语言对，文字与语言身份混淆；仅1B规模、30B token、每配置单一种子；仅研究以英语为锚的双语设定与高资源语言，未涵盖非英语间迁移与真正多语场景。

Abstract: Tokenization represents one of the most crucial steps in mulilingual NLP pipelines. Yet, tokenizers routinely under-allocate vocabulary to low-resource languages. While improved allocation leads to better performance, it remains poorly understood how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations and transfer during pretraining. To address this, we pretrain 39 mono- and bilingual 1B decoder-only models on FineWeb2-HQ across English, German, French, Arabic and Chinese, varying only the tokenizer. Our results demonstrate that improved vocabulary allocation (i) substantially raises cross-lingual representation alignment in early-to-mid layers, an effect that prior work measuring only the output layer could not observe, (ii) increases cross-lingual parametric knowledge sharing in feed-forward neurons, supported by correlational and causal evidence, and (iii) an alignment-transfer dissociation, where cross-lingual transfer remains essentially unchanged despite higher alignment. Moreover, transfer is significantly lower for cross-script bilinguals even under fair vocabulary allocation, indicating that the script barrier is not merely a tokenizer artifact. All of our checkpoints and code are publicly available.

</details>


### [21] [The Assistant Persona Differs Across Languages in Activation Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27504)
*Daniel Yoo,Naama Rozen,Evan Harris*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文在 Qwen3-32B 的 31 种语言中分别提取"助手轴"（Assistant Axis，即默认助手状态与角色扮演状态在残差流空间中的差分方向），发现各语言的助手轴方向差异显著（与英语轴余弦相似度仅 0.378–0.911，均值 0.743），且轴方向、轴范数、默认状态在英语轴上的投影均随语言资源量（Common Crawl 页面占比）单调变化（ρ=0.774/0.904/0.831）；低资源语言的默认状态更靠近"角色扮演极"，用英语标定的激活截断（capping）阈值会错误地大幅抬升其投影；沿本语言轴的反向 steering 比沿英语轴更能放大人格化越狱（AIM+MultiJail，9 语言，负系数下高 2.1 个百分点）。结论是模型并不存在跨语言统一的助手表征，多语言对齐需要把助手人格显式作为干预目标。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 已有大量行为层面证据表明大模型在英语之外的安全性显著下降（将有害请求翻译为低资源语言会大幅提高依从率，多语言安全干预在低资源语言中效果更差），但这些差异背后的机制尚不清楚。机制可解释性工作已发现"拒绝方向"和"人格向量"可被提取、监控与操控，Lu et al. (2026) 进一步定义了分离默认助手状态与角色扮演状态的 Assistant Axis 并用于 monitoring/steering/activation capping，但这些方向几乎全部从英语中提取并被默认假设可跨语言迁移。同时 multilingual 表征既有共享成分（refusal 方向跨语言近似平行）也有语言特定成分（低资源语言的 probing 方向相似度更低）的相互矛盾的证据，因此需要直接检验 Assistant Axis 的跨语言几何一致性。

Method: 模型：主实验 Qwen3-32B，附录在 Gemma 2 27B、Llama 3.3 70B 上复现主要趋势。语言：Deng et al. (2024) 的 31 种，按 2024-11 Common Crawl 页面占比分为高资源(>1%，11 种)、中资源(0.1–1%，10 种)、低资源(<0.1%，9 种)。Assistant Axis 提取：复刻 Lu et al. (2026) 流程——用翻译后的角色扮演 system prompt + 50 条统一提取问题（随机采样 30 个角色）生成回复，GPT-4.1-mini 作为裁判按 0–3 打分（是否完全扮演角色），仅用评分 3 的回复在响应 token 上平均得到角色向量；用无 system prompt 的同组问题得到默认助手状态；轴 = 默认状态均值 − 角色向量均值（在 layer 32 报告）。翻译：所有 system prompt 与问题由 GPT-5.6 Sol 在单次调用中译入 30 种语言。干预：在选定层加 α·v̂（正 α 指向助手极，负 α 指向角色扮演极），α 按各语言平均残差流范数标定；jailbreak 集为 AIM persona 前缀 + MultiJail（9 语言 × 315 条），由 GPT-5.6 Luna 按 harmfulness 与 generation degradation 打分。Activation capping：沿轴投影设下限，阈值取标定 rollout 的 25 百分位；对各语言默认状态在 layer 46–53 投影与英语阈值 τ 的差值做比较。分析工具：Jacobian lens（Gurnee et al. 2026，残差流到 unembedding 的 Jacobian 平均 + 梯度追踪稀疏分解与词表 token 排序），附录另有 SAE（Neuronpedia）与 logit lens。控制变量：Common Crawl 占比 vs ASJP 词汇距离回归、tokenizer fertility 回归、按残差流范数归一化、响应长度截断至 96 token、去裁判过滤重建轴、per-layer 分析、persona vector 替代管线。

### [23] [Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27721)

TL;DR: 本文首次在多语言情感分类任务上系统对比了三个“决策模型”（Jev、OpenAI Decisions、Strands Decider 2B）、两个通用大模型（GPT-6 Luna、Qwen3.5-2B）与两个微调编码器（tabularisai、XLM-EMO），覆盖 10 个数据集、5 种语言、4 类情绪，并配对检验差异与等价性。结论：无标注数据时，三个最强零样本系统（Jev、OpenAI Decisions、GPT-6 Luna）平均仅比域内微调低约 1 个 macro-F1 点，但统计上无法排除 4–5 点差距；它们明显优于“跨数据集微调”的编码器（+15 点 vs tabularisai、+8 点 vs XLM-EMO）；“决策格式”本身不提升质量，只带来约 5 倍的更低延迟、逐选项概率和（匹配条件下）更好的校准。

  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 决策模型（decision models）是 2026 年 9–10 月集中出现的一类新接口形态：输入问题与封闭候选选项集合，输出各选项概率而非自由文本，厂商宣称低延迟、对提示措辞鲁棒。此前唯一相关研究 Emo-Jev 只评估了单一决策模型、只做单次运行、无置信区间与显著性检验，且早于决策模型出现。既有零样本 LLM 与微调模型的比较研究多使用较早模型、单一提示、未做等价性检验，并指出 LLM 在细粒度情感任务上通常落后于微调模型，且对提示措辞和选项顺序敏感。因此需要一项受控、多语言、带不确定性量化与统计检验的比较，回答三个问题：(H1) 零样本系统能否取代需要标注数据的微调；(H2) 复用其他数据集微调模型是否可靠、零样本是否更好；(H3) 决策模型相对通用 LLM 在质量与延迟上是否更优；(H4) 零样本系统对提示措辞与选项顺序是否鲁棒。

Method: 任务：从社交媒体短文本中四选一（joy/sadness/anger/fear），指标为 macro-F1（1 点 = 0.01 macro-F1）。数据：10 个公开数据集、5 语言（英/德/西/法/意），66,619 文本，测试集 12,633；剔除多标签文本（5,237 条主要来自 SemEval-2018），GoEmotions 按官方映射折叠为 Ekman 基本情绪；按文本归一化键分组防止重复泄漏。系统：5 个零样本系统（Jev API、OpenAI Decisions /v1/decisions、Strands Decider 2B、GPT-6 Luna、Qwen3.5-2B），每个跑 4 个提示变体（措辞+选项顺序，顺序构成拉丁方），意大利语指令，另加英语与文本语言指令的补充实验；两个微调参考编码器（tabularisai 基于 XLM-R，XLM-EMO 基于 XLM-T）在每个数据集训练划分上分别微调（3 个随机种子），构成“训练→测试”矩阵：对角线为域内（in），非对角线平均为跨域（out），公共 checkpoint 原样使用为 zs。统计：组自助重采样（B=10,000，按文本组重采样，所有系统配对）、Holm 多重比较校正、TOST 等价性检验（主等价边际 δ=0.02，另报 0.01/0.03）、最小等价边际 δ_min、精确 Wilcoxon 符号秩检验、随机效应元分析（REML + Hartung–Knapp，95% 预测区间，I² 异质性），并按数据集加权方式做稳健性分析。补充实验：标签打分（label scoring）给通用 LLM 产出决策式概率以分离“格式”与“训练”效应；受控单请求延迟测量；二次运行分解提示效应与运行间随机性；温度缩放重校准与 ECE/多类 Brier 校准评估；置换检验与位置偏置测量。所有 per-text 预测与脚本将公开。

Result: 平均 macro-F1：Jev 0.708、OpenAI Decisions 0.707、GPT-6 Luna 0.706、Strands 2B 0.669、Qwen3.5-2B 0.571；tabularisai_in 0.717、tabularisai_out 0.553、XLM-EMO_in 0.690（8 集）、XLM-EMO_out 0.596；公共 checkpoint 0.525/0.616。(H1) 三个领先零样本系统平均落后域内微调约 0.9–1.0 点，90% CI 宽 0.039–0.049，无法在 ±2 点内证明等价（δ_min 0.039–0.049，若真差为 0 需测试集扩大 4–7 倍），结论为“不确定”；Strands 2B（−4.8）与 Qwen3.5-2B（−14.5）显著更差。数据集间异质性极大（I²≈0.97，τ≈0.085，新数据集 95% 预测区间 [−0.22, +0.20]）：零样本在 BRIGHTER 显著领先 13–16 点，在 GoEmotions 显著落后 17–22 点（joy 标注惯例差异），优势随训练集规模增大而扩大（探索性 Spearman −0.62~−0.88）。(H2) 编码器跨域显著退化（tabularisai −16.3 点、XLM-EMO −9.5 点）；零样本系统对 tabularisai_out 领先 11.5–15.5 点（随机效应亦显著），对 XLM-EMO_out 领先 4–9 点但仅在本数据集上成立（Wilcoxon 与随机效应不显著）。XLM-EMO 跨域微调后（0.596）反而低于其未微调公共 checkpoint（0.616）。探索性对比：零样本领先最强公共模型约 6 点（vs XLM-EMO_zs），领先 tabularisai_zs 约 18 点。(H3) OpenAI Decisions 与 GPT-6 Luna 质量等价（Δ=+0.001，1 点内即等价），中位延迟 229 ms vs 1,107 ms（约 1/5），受控顺序测量比值 5.38 [5.10,5.64]；Strands 2B 比同规模 Qwen3.5-2B 高 9.7 点，标签打分显示该优势来自决策适配器训练与从 Qwen3.5-4B 的部分蒸馏，而非决策格式；Strands 2B 与 4B 教师在 2 点内等价，且约快 3 倍、提示敏感度减半；API 成本均约 $0.02/千次请求，无法区分。(H4) 领先系统跨提示 SD 0.008–0.013（稳定），Strands 2B 0.012（临界，不确定），Qwen3.5-2B 0.073（拒绝，位置偏置 +10.6 个百分点）；指令语言（意大利语/英语/文本语言）对领先系统影响 <1 点，但小模型用文本语言指令可提升 6.2 点并降低位置偏置。校准：决策模型 ECE 0.088–0.098 优于域内编码器 0.129–0.134，重校准后域内差异消失、跨域决策模型仍更好；匹配比较中 Strands 2B 优于标签打分 Qwen3.5-2B（ECE 0.088 vs 0.104，Brier 0.301 vs 0.403）。

Conclusion: 决策格式本身不增加质量：OpenAI Decisions 与其底层 GPT-6 Luna 等效，标签打分给通用 LLM 同样的输出格式也不改变质量与不稳定性；Strands 2B 相对同规模通用 LLM 的 10 点优势应归因于其决策适配器训练与蒸馏，而非格式。决策格式真正带来的是速度（决策 API 约快 5 倍，标签打分亦快于生成）、在通用 LLM API 不返回概率时提供逐选项概率，以及在同规模匹配比较中更好的校准；成本无法区分 API 系统。无目标域标注数据时，三个领先零样本系统（Jev、OpenAI Decisions、GPT-6 Luna）是稳健且强的默认选择——它们优于跨域微调模型，也（探索性地）优于最强公共情感模型；但“与域内微调持平”不能被等价性检验支持，且在新数据集上二者可能互有胜负。标注数据充足时微调可能更优，其优势仅在最大的 GoEmotions 上明显，且无法区分是规模效应还是标注惯例效应。作者强调数据集间异质性（单集差异可达 ±22 点）使均值极易被误读，建议此类比较报告 per-dataset 配对差异、显式等价边际与对应检验、新数据集预测区间、多提示变体与平衡选项顺序，并使用基于同一基座的 label scoring 对照以分离格式与训练效应。局限包括仅 4 类单标签任务、指令语言、提示变体数少、闭源系统版本漂移与不可验证成本、部分分析与假设非预注册。

Abstract: Decision models receive a question with a closed list of answers and return a probability for each answer instead of free text. They promise low latency and robustness to prompt wording, but no study has compared several of them with fine-tuned encoders across languages. We ask whether systems used without training on labelled data (zero-shot) can replace fine-tuning, and what the decision format adds over a general-purpose large language model (LLM). We compare three decision models (Jev, OpenAI Decisions, Strands Decider 2B) and two LLMs (GPT-6 Luna, Qwen3.5-2B), given Italian instructions, with two fine-tuned multilingual encoders (tabularisai, XLM-EMO) on four emotions (joy, sadness, anger, fear) in 10 social-media datasets in five languages, with paired difference and equivalence tests. The three best zero-shot systems (two decision models and one LLM) score on average about one macro-F1 point below an encoder fine-tuned on the target dataset; our test sets cannot exclude a gap of 4-5 points, and on single datasets either approach wins by up to 22 points. They beat encoders fine-tuned on another dataset by 8-15 points, though against XLM-EMO this may not extend to new datasets, and instructions in each text's language change their results by under 1 point. Exploratorily, they beat the strongest public emotion model used as is by about 6 points. OpenAI's decision endpoint matches GPT-6 Luna, the LLM it runs on, at a fifth of its median latency, and a 2-billion-parameter decision model beats a same-size general LLM by 10 points, owing to its training, not the decision format. The best zero-shot systems, the LLM included, have an SD of about 1 point across prompts. Without labelled data they are a strong default, and decision models add lower latency and, unlike generative LLM use, per-option probabilities. Fine-tuning won by a wide margin only on the largest dataset, GoEmotions.

### [24] [RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27750)
*Junying Wang,Yijin Guo,Yalun Wu,Ziheng Jiao,Farong Wen,Qihang Yan,Wenzhe Li,Ye Shen,Qi Jia,Chunyi Li,Zicheng Zhang,Guangtao Zhai*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: RoSci 论文提出"科学模型鲁棒性"概念，构建了包含 1,220 个退化样本的诊断基准 RoSci-Bench（涵盖信息错误与信息丢失两大维度、六种退化类型），并提出基于 Parse-Verify-Decide 流程的 RoSci-Agent。实验显示 20 个 VLM 在退化输入下频繁给出错误答案或幻觉前提，最佳独立模型总分仅 31.95，而 RoSci-Agent 达到 44.77，显著优于所有基线（bootstrap 95% CI 42.51–47.15 vs 基线 ≤34.60），并具备跨骨干模型的通用增益。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有科学多模态推理基准（如 ScienceQA、MMMU、MathVista、ChartQA）普遍假设模型面对的是完整、准确的输入，忽略了真实科研场景中普遍存在的数据错误与信息缺失：人类研究者遇到前提矛盾或条件不足时会暂停推理、复核假设或质疑条件，而 VLM 往往自信地基于幻觉前提作答（如图 1：图表只有紫色柱却被问及蓝色柱，模型虚构蓝柱回答 2；圆周角题只给 20° 却把答案翻倍为 40°）。已有鲁棒性工作多聚焦"信号级"感知扰动（图像噪声、遮挡、视觉腐蚀）或语义层面的引导性/错误前提问题，缺乏面向科学"逻辑级"前提有效性的系统评测；同时，现有可靠性增强方法（选择性预测、滞后自我修正如 VL-Rethinker、Sherlock）本质是"先生成再调试"，在未经验证的基础上纠错。因此需要一个统一的测试床，检验模型何时该作答、何时该请求澄清、何时该拒绝科学问题。

Method: 概念层面：定义 Scientific Model Robustness，包含 Information Error Robustness（识别事实错误、逻辑矛盾、跨模态冲突并拒绝不当推断）与 Information Loss Robustness（识别缺失/不完整条件并表达不确定或弃答）。基准构建：①样本采集——从 MathVista、Super-CLEVR、AI2D、FigureQA、UniGeo、Geometry3K、MV-Math 等筛选 305 道需图文共同参与、覆盖物理/化学/生物/数学的源问题；②退化设计——领域专家注入六类退化：MFE（轻微事实错误）、CFE（关键事实错误）、VOL（违反定律/方法）、CMC（跨模态矛盾，如文本改 100kg 而图仍标 10kg）、CFL（关键事实缺失，如删除时间 t）、CIL（多图场景关键图像缺失）；③类比扩展——用 GPT-5 作改写引擎为每个种子生成 3 个语义等价但表层上下文/数值不同的变体，共 305+305×3=1,220 样本；④质量保证——专家审查、难度过滤、可解性验证。评测体系：将数据划分为可解子集 D_sol 与不可解子集 D_unsol，采用三面仲裁协议（LLM-as-a-Judge 给出推理稳定性 S_stab、拒答 F1（F1_rej）、拒绝理由质量 S_just，再综合为 0/1/2 整体分并线性缩放到 0–100）。Agent 层面：RoSci-Agent 采用三阶段 Parse-Verify-Decide 流程——Stage I 知识解析（KP，用 VLM 将图像 I 与问题 Q 转为含目标/已知条件/约束/图表元数据的 JSON 结构化知识 K）、Stage II 信息验证（IV，双路径：信息错误检测检查跨模态一致性与科学定律，信息损失检测检查求解所需变量是否齐备，输出带 checkpoint ID、PASS/FAIL 状态与证据的验证结果集 V）、Stage III 策略生成（SG，按加权异常分 S_anomaly=Σ w_k·I(v_k=FAIL) 与阈值 τ_refuse、τ_clarify 决定 Reject / Clarify / Answer）。权重按严重度设定（MFE 0.3、CFE 0.7、VOL/CMC/CFL/CIL 1.0），阈值与权重在 20% 留出验证集上网格搜索，以最大化不可答拒答 F1 且可解任务准确率下降不超过 δ 为约束。骨干模型为 GPT-5，并另在 Claude-3.7-Sonnet、Gemini-2.5-Pro 上验证通用性。

Result: （1）人类专家总分 98.90，远高于最佳独立 VLM 的 31.95，凸显巨大差距。（2）20 个模型中最佳者为 Claude-4-Sonnet-Thinking（31.95）与 Claude-3.7-Sonnet（30.21），带思考与不带思考模型的整体分高度重叠；多数基线在 Information Loss 上得分低于 Information Error（8 个基线中 7 个如此，仅 GPT-5 例外）。（3）RoSci-Agent 总分 44.77，超过所有基线；在 IE/IL 两个方向的整体分（44.7/45.0）均为最高，Stability 61.62、Rejection F1 51.17、Justification 55.80，在 CFL 上拒答 F1 达 35.00、Stability 47.50，优于基线最高值 25.00/42.50 等。（4）跨骨干通用性：Claude-3.7-Sonnet +13.64、Gemini-2.5-Pro +15.36、GPT-5 +23.53，平均 +14.50。（5）Bootstrap（N=305, K=1000）显示 RoSci 95% CI 下界 42.51 高于所有基线上界（≤34.60）。（6）SRCC 分析显示 Overall 与 Information Error 相关性（0.954）远强于与 Information Loss（0.390），IE 与 IL 的模型排名弱相关（ρ=0.191），CFL 与 CIL 仅 0.281，验证两维度需独立评估。（7）效率上 RoSci-Agent 约 1,850 token，优于 Self-Consistency(k=5) 的约 2,600 token，且总分更高（44.77 vs 33.45）。（8）LLM-as-a-Judge（GPT-4o）与专家判定在 150 条抽样上一致率约 92.7%（TP 42.0%、FP 5.3%、FN 2.0%、TN 50.7%）。

Conclusion: RoSci 首次系统提出并量化 Scientific Model Robustness，交付 1,220 样本的 RoSci-Bench（六类退化、约 980 信息错误 / 240 信息丢失，跨模态矛盾占比最大约 556，可解约 240 / 不可解约 960），将科学多模态评测的范式从"理想条件下的推理能力"扩展到"前提有效性与可解性判断"。RoSci-Agent 通过先验证前提再做推理，把"生成后纠错"转为"推理前校验"，显著提升拒答与理由质量并获得 bootstrap 统计显著性，同时在三个骨干模型上均有效，证明该机制与具体模型无关。局限与展望方面：模型整体鲁棒性（44.77）与专家（98.90）仍有巨大差距，信息损失维度仍是普遍短板；基准变体由 GPT-5 改写生成，可能引入改写偏差；判分依赖 LLM-as-a-Judge（一致率 92.7%）；阈值与权重需针对验证集调参；未来可扩展更多学科、更长链推理任务及更自动化的变体生成与人类标注复核。

Abstract: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable significant progress in scientific tasks. However, these models are generally assumed to be presented with complete and accurate information, overlooking the challenges of erroneous/missing information in wild scenarios. To address this gap, we introduce the concept of Scientific Model Robustness, which defines a model's ability to detect anomalies, assess solvability, and perform self-calibration when faced with Information Error (inconsistencies) or Information Loss (insufficiency). Specifically, we present RoSci-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,220 samples using a seed-variant strategy across six degradation types. To address VLM fragility, we further propose RoSci-Agent, a framework that employs a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline to vet premises before reasoning. The evaluated VLMs sometimes answer questions whose premises are invalid or incomplete. RoSci-Agent achieves a higher Overall Robustness Score than the evaluated standalone VLMs. RoSci-Bench gives the multimodal reasoning community a common test of when models answer, request clarification, or reject a scientific question.

</details>


### [25] [How Much of a Calculation-Error Rate Is Not Arithmetic: Auditing the FinReason Cup 2026 Task 3 Metric with a Deterministic Rule System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27192)
*Vladimir Beskorovainyi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: FinReason Cup 2026 任务3（XBRL 财务审计验证）的"计算错误率"CER 名不副实：由于评测采用层级标签（先判结构/抽取，再判计算），而被错误接受的"报告值"会把案例推入计算错误列；加之 DQC_US_0015 规则的参考答案恒为报告值的相反数（110/110 练习样例精确成立），这类案例的计算值根本不含算术内容。作者用公开榜单的"分规则准确率 + 错误类别率"做减法，得到下界：23 个参赛队中 22 个下界为正，最高的两个并列第一队至少 11/12 与 12/13 的计算错误"不是算术"，即榜首系统约 92% 的计算错误并非算术错。承载该论证的系统是一个纯确定性规则系统（重建 DQC_US_0015/0117/0126 三条规则，无学习参数、无训练、无外部服务），开发集 96.62%（离线确定性裁判）、测试集 95.29%，全部 680 例 1.4 秒跑完。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 任务3（Financial Audit Verification）对每个案例给出两个值：实例文档中的报告值（extracted_value）与计算关系所蕴含的计算值（calculated_value），并按层级规则打标签：答案不是合法双键对象→S（结构错）；报告值与文件不符→E（抽取错）；报告值正确但计算值不符→C（计算错）；两者都对→A（正确）。ACC 为主指标，SER/EER/CER 报告失败来源。作者指出两个层面的问题：(1) 指标层面：由于分层标签机制，任何"报告值本身错误却被接受"的案例都会被记入计算错误列，因此公开的 CER 无法被读者分解为"算术失败"与"选错事实失败"；而基准所用的三条 DQC 规则中，DQC_US_0015（Negative Values）的正确答案就是报告值的相反数，一旦事实选定就不再有算术可错，C 标签记录的是"错事实/错路径"而非"错求和"。(2) 建设层面：参赛者只有练习集有答案、排行榜阶段答案不公开，任何设计选择的检验都只能消耗每日提交额度，因此需要一套可解释、可复算的确定性系统来暴露指标问题。

Method: 方法由两条线组成。第一条线是"作为载体的系统"：一条纯标准库 Python 3.10 确定性流水线，无学习参数、无逐案硬编码分支、无外部服务。流程为——解析实例文档为事实（概念、上下文/期间/维度成员、数值），解析计算 linkbase 为按扩展链接角色的带权父子关系；再按三条 DQC 规则分别走专属路径：DQC_US_0015 取"应为非负"的负值事实（先非维度负值事实，再取维度事实并剔除规则排除的成员/轴），答案取报告值取反；DQC_US_0117 取某轴上成员事实之和（轴候选取自规则轴表，取与报告值偏离最大者；当定义 linkbase 未声明层级时用"等于其余成员之和"的成员视为小计予以剔除，即自创的 subtotal fix），并以第二断言（成员自身事实与二次轴分解比较）作兜底；DQC_US_0126 取治理角色下计算子项的有符号和（角色按实际报告子项数排序确定）。当所有路径都得不到与报告值不同的值时退化为符号取反（猜测，非计算）。当同一概念同期间有多个候选事实时按"维度成员名排序"选择参考事实。第二条线是"指标审计"：利用官方公开的每队分规则准确率（推得各规则错误数 e_15）与 SER/EER（推得结构+抽取标签总数 S+E），计算下界 bound = e_15 − (S+E)，即"至少有多少计算错误落在计算值由报告值决定的案例上"；并做三重自洽校验（每条公开数值恰好对应唯一整数、逐行两法求和一致、误差分类与规则计数均为 32/680）。此外用同一 680 例官方"规则基线"在两个裁判（确定性裁判 vs 官方 gpt-5-mini / finmr-judge-v1）下的分数做对比，量化裁判间系统性分歧；并用 Arelle + XBRL US xule 引擎、语言模型探针、排行榜"故意破坏抽取"的两次提交探针来检验残余错误成因与实践集/规则引擎的代理可靠性。

Result: 系统与成绩：开发集确定性裁判 96.62%（657/680 正确，15 抽取错 + 8 计算错），官方裁判 96.32%；测试集 95.29%，并列第 15/23，SER 0.15%、EER 1.03%、CER 3.53%（1 结构 + 7 抽取 + 24 计算错，共 32 错）。开发集上 461 例走子项求和、161 例走 DQC_US_0015 取反、57 例走 DQC_US_0117 成员求和。全流程 1.4 秒、峰值内存 113 MB。分规则错误分布：测试集 18（DQC_US_0015/162 例）、9（0117/54）、5（0126/464）；榜首队为 14、1、0，差距按规则分解为 4、8、5 例，且恰位于系统未复现规则作用域约束的部分。指标审计结论：110/110 练习案例中 DQC_US_0015 的参考计算值 = 参考报告值的相反数（对照 0117 为 1/120、0126 为 6/102）；由于每案仅一个标签、总共只有 8 个结构/抽取标签，本队 18 个 DQC_US_0015 错中至少 10 个必属计算错误 ⇒ 24 个计算错误中至少 10 个不是算术；榜首两队分别至少 ≥11/12 与 ≥12/13，约为 92%；下界对 23 队中 22 队为正，对 9 队覆盖其计算错误的一半以上；无任何队伍在 DQC_US_0015 上超过 91.98%，且每队至少 13 错。裁判分歧：同一官方基线上官方裁判比确定性裁判少 47 个抽取错、多 37 个计算错、多 9 个正确，净差给出"至少 46 例至多 74 例"的区间；且官方"确定性分数是官方分数下界"的通则被本系统反例推翻（96.62% vs 96.32%）。另外：练习集实例文档过半被截断、132/332 例所问事实根本不在所发文本中（可答上限 60.24%），练习集与测试集规则构成严重错配（0117 占 36% vs 8%，0126 占 31% vs 68%），一次"实践集+规则引擎一致"的改动提交后反而从 96.62% 降到 96.47%（差 1 例）而被回滚；官方分数从 96.32% 降到 95.29%（约 1.4 个标准误，作者称为与过拟合一致但非证据）。残余错误集中在"同一概念同期间有多个同样被标记的事实、而问题未指明维度成员"的案例，开发集涉及 31/680 例：实践集上按成员名排序在 17 个多候重组中命中 14（去前缀 16，事实 ID 排序 13），第二次排行榜探针在 31 例中至少命中 21 例（均匀期望 10.7、σ=2.4），而 15 例子集上的第一次探针仅至少 5 例（期望 5.2，与随机不可区分）。

Conclusion: 核心结论：层级式评测下的"计算错误率"无法报告其名义所指——每个"被接受但错误"的报告值都会落入计算列，因此阅读者无法区分算术失败与选错事实；而分规则准确率不受重标注影响，可仅凭公开数字界定影响：本队 32 个测试错中 18 个落在 DQC_US_0015，其答案在全部 110 个已公布练习案例中恒为报告值的相反数（并据规则定义推断在排名阶段同样成立——这是整节论证唯一依赖的前提），在仅有 1 个结构与 7 个抽取标签的情况下，24 个计算错误中至少 10 个所在案例已无算术可错；该下界对 23 队中 22 队为正，且在系统最强的榜首处最紧（约 92% 的计算错误并非算术）。因此建议基准方：(1) 在层级式数字之外，另对"报告值与参考答案一致"的子集单独计算值得分，二者并列即可零额外标注成本地分离两类失败；(2) 继续公布分规则准确率；(3) 消除选择歧义——把维度成员写入问题，或整组给出 finding 而非单个幸存事实（开发集上影响 31/680 例）。对参赛者的可迁移教训是程序性的：练习集规则构成与排名阶段相差 28～37 个百分点、排名答案不公开因而无法构造留出集，每次设计检验都要消耗提交额度，故额度是稀缺资源，应在开工前就规划预算，而非像本文这样消耗在自认为正确的改动上；同时"实践集一致 + 规则引擎裁定"并不足以免除提交，引擎在所发文件上的结论与基准参考答案并不可互换。系统本身可复现（标准库、1.4 秒、逐行输出与机制计数可完全重现），但作者暂不公开源码；引擎核对用 Arelle 3.0.30055 + xule 插件、dqc_us_rules master 分支（2026 年 10 月读取），因排除清单随规则版本变化，复读者应固定版本。

Abstract: Task 3 of the FinReason Cup 2026 scores a system on two values per case, the one an XBRL filing reports and the one its own calculation relationships imply, and labels each failure as structural, extraction or calculation. This report shows that the calculation-error rate so defined does not count arithmetic failures, and bounds how far it is from one using the published board alone. One of the three rules behind the benchmark, DQC_US_0015, has an answer that is the negation of the reported value (in all 110 published practice cases, against 1 of 120 and 6 of 102 for the other two), so a calculation label on such a case records a wrong fact or a wrong route, not a wrong sum. Subtracting the available structural and extraction labels from each entry's error count on that rule gives a floor: the bound is positive for 22 of the 23 ranked entries, and at the top it is sharpest, with at least 11 of 12 and 12 of 13 calculation errors of the two joint-first entries falling on cases where no arithmetic remained. The calculation-error rate of the best systems on this task is almost entirely not arithmetic. The vehicle for that result is an entry that reconstructs the three data-quality rules the benchmark is drawn from, DQC_US_0015, DQC_US_0117 and DQC_US_0126, as a deterministic system with no learned parameters, no training step and no external service, running all 680 cases in 1.4 seconds. It scores 96.62% under the offline judge on development and 95.29% on the published test set, and its residual error concentrates in cases where a concept carries several equally flagged facts and the question names no dimensional member. Reading those error classes against the per-rule accuracies is what exposed the metric, which is why both are reported here.

</details>


### [26] [Neural Geometry as a Learning Signal](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26832)
*Eric Todd,Tal Haklay,Nikhil Prakash,Matthew Finlayson,Michael Hanna,Fenil R. Doshi,Daniel Wurgaft,Thomas McGrath,Owen Lewis,David Bau,Jack Merullo,Ekdeep Singh Lubana,Matthew Kowal,Thomas Fel,Atticus Geiger*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We investigate whether the geometric structure of neural representations can provide a sufficient learning signal for improving model behavior without any supervision on model outputs. First, we fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B to answer questions such as "What month is four months after June?" by supervising internal representations of the input month (June = 6) and offset (4), which are encoded with Fourier harmonics. Second, we fine-tune the model to predict line breaks in text wrapped to a fixed width by supervising an internal representation of the number of characters since the preceding newline, which is represented by a low-dimensional helical structure. In both tasks, we supervise a low-dimensional subspace of the residual stream using an idealized target structure, and find that internal geometric supervision achieves similar performance to standard fine-tuning (despite no supervision on outputs). Moreover, we find that simply patching in an ideal geometry is not sufficient to recover fine-tuning performance, and thus demonstrate geometric supervision provides beneficial effects beyond the representations it targets. Together, these findings show how mechanistic understanding of neural geometry can be leveraged to shape the behavior of neural networks.

### [27] [LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26863)
*Anirudh Atmakuru,Tanya Goyal*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. In this paper, we study the consequences of directly adopting reasoning-centric training recipes, e.g., the use of outcome-based rewards for reinforcement learning (RL), injection of "cognitive" behaviors such as proposing and backtracking from hypotheses in reasoning chains, etc., for knowledge tasks. We hypothesize that these decisions, while useful for reasoning, inadvertently encourage models to memorize hallucinations they themselves generate in their long reasoning chains when trained on knowledge tasks. To study this, we train models with standard post-training, extract their self-generated hallucinations during RL, and track memorization throughout the rest of training. Our experiments on six open models across two model families and two architectures confirm our hypothesis. We find that models' recall of hallucinations reinforced during training increases by 4.83% on average, compared to just 0.17% for self-hallucinations that receive no training signal. In fact, models even memorize false facts that they immediately retract in their reasoning; a backtracking template inherited from reasoning-centric training that has no benefit for knowledge recall. Furthermore, we find that memorization is strongest on the hardest training questions, and rewarding a hallucination makes the model less likely to abstain from it later (by 7.23% on average). Overall, our work identifies and systematically studies a previously unexamined pathway through which models learn hallucinations during training.

### [28] [How Language Models Compress and Compare: Understanding Selection with Token Covariance Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26874)
*Moshe Eliasof*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Many language-model tasks reduce to selecting among structured alternatives, yet we still lack a simple picture of how a decoder-only transformer organizes an entire selection prompt across depth. We introduce token covariance maps, a prompt-level geometric view that tracks how token positions co-vary in hidden-state space at each layer. This turns a structured prompt into a depth-indexed sequence of maps whose spectral and block structure can be aligned with instructions, context, and candidate answers. Across 14 decoder-only models from 4 families and 12 structured-selection benchmarks, token covariance maps reveal a robust compress-then-compare organization. Early layers represent prompts diffusely, middle layers compress them into a shared low-rank bottleneck, and late layers re-expand into context-option and option-option geometry. This organization recurs across larger fixed-template samples, deterministic prompt rewrites, pairwise reranking reformulations, and controlled answer-set manipulations, while also emerging during training from an initially flat depth profile. Its timing aligns with behavior: useful answer discrimination appears well after the bottleneck, and low-rank intervention around the bottleneck preferentially disrupts late comparison geometry. We additionally show that the same geometric profile appears in instruction-tuned models, across several languages, and during open-ended generation. We further show that changing the internal representation of one candidate around the compressed region can shift which candidate the model later prefers. These results show that token covariance maps are a diagnostic tool for comparing how models organize information across prompts, model families, and stages of training.

### [29] [ORBIT: Offset-based Activation Steering for Cross-lingual Multimodal Fact Verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27421)
*Huy Trieu,Duy-Minh Nguyen-Tran,Thanh-Dat Nguyen,Huy Tien Nguyen,Tung Le*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multimodal fact verification faces a fundamental accessibility bottleneck: while large proprietary models exhibit cross-lingual robustness, small vision-language models suffer a severe, disproportionate accuracy collapse on low-resource languages. Closing this gap traditionally requires prohibitive scale or extensive language-specific fine-tuning. In this work, we propose Offset Recovery via Bilingual Inference-time Technique (ORBIT), an algorithmic intervention that mitigates this collapse at inference time. ORBIT estimates span-specific offset vectors from parallel claim-evidence instances and applies them to claim and evidence representations, targeting the cross-lingual degradation induced by low-resource evidence. Experiments across 81 configurations reveal that ORBIT substantially recovers both accuracy and F1-score in low-resource settings, exposes calibration offset norms as a diagnostic proxy, and outperforms translation-based and steering baselines.

### [30] [Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27607)
*Zayd Muhammad Kawakibi Zuhri,Munachiso Samuel Nwadike,Kentaro Inui,Alham Fikri Aji*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We introduce Tasklets, a benchmark of small synthetic tasks for evaluating the computational capabilities of language model sequence-mixing layers. These tasks probe foundational capabilities such as recall, sequence manipulation, and state tracking. Such tasks are widely used in architecture research, but differences in task selection, formulation, and evaluation make comparisons across studies difficult. Tasklets brings these tasks together, organizing them by the capabilities they test and providing a shared setup for evaluating how different architectural layer types learn fundamental computations. We compare a broad range of layer types through controlled experiments with small models. Our task implementations and evaluation code support reproducible, low-cost testing of new architectural proposals: this https URL .

### [31] [SkillPrivus: Uncovering PRIVacy of USe Harms in Agentic Skills](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26747)
*Mariana Fernandez-Espinosa,Ivoline Ngong,Keerthiram Murugesan,Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Agent skills extend AI assistants through installable instructions and code that can access users' files, accounts, and data. Even when performing their advertised tasks, skills may infer sensitive attributes, retain unnecessary information, or disclose data to unexpected recipients. We study these potential privacy-of-use harms through SkillPrivus, a static audit framework that analyzes skills before installation without executing them. SkillPrivus extracts data operations from code and natural-language instructions, grounds them in source evidence, and adapts Contextual Integrity to assess their appropriateness. Applied to 726 real skills from public marketplaces, 563 of which handle personal data, SkillPrivus flags at least one potential violation in 307 of these skills (54.5%), and its judgments agree with three blind human annotators on 83.2% of resolvable moves. The flagged behaviors include sensitive inferences, information use beyond the stated task, and disclosures to unexpected recipients, suggesting that privacy harms can arise from ordinary skill functionality.

### [32] [Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26756)
*Anika Misra,Shreyas Vinod,Huteng Dai*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We show that reinforcement learning (RL) in reasoning tasks can succeed even when the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data is severely corrupted. In a mathematical reasoning dataset (GSM8K), we systematically corrupt training trajectories across 361 configurations by injecting realistic error types, varying error locations, trace-answer consistency, and corruption ratios up to 100%. While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels (approximately 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N = 8 minimal, incorrect, three-line "form-only" traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%). Further, we show that SFT accuracy is largely uncorrelated with post-RL accuracy (r approximately 0), demonstrating a fundamental asymmetry in post-training: SFT primarily establishes structural layout (form), while RL independently discovers functional reasoning (function).

Abstract: We show that reinforcement learning (RL) in reasoning tasks can succeed even when the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data is severely corrupted. In a mathematical reasoning dataset (GSM8K), we systematically corrupt training trajectories across 361 configurations by injecting realistic error types, varying error locations, trace-answer consistency, and corruption ratios up to 100%. While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels (approximately 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N = 8 minimal, incorrect, three-line "form-only" traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%). ### [33] [Know Your Context Bank: Repairing Inconsistency and Measuring Generalization in Context-Aware Text-to-SQL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26775)
*Hailong Li,Mohammadreza Pourreza,Tal Neiman,Reza Sherkat,Per Jacobsson,Yannis Papakonstantinou*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Text-to-SQL systems increasingly rely on context banks: curated collections of example queries, metric definitions, and domain knowledge that tell a model how an organization writes its queries. In the enterprise, a bank grows over years as many analysts add entries, checked one at a time for correctness (does the SQL answer its own question?) and rarely for consistency with one another. Yet correctness is often loosely defined: a question seldom fixes how an entity is counted or which table defines it, so two entries can each pass review yet resolve the same decision in opposite ways. We call this condition context bank rot. A second question follows: does a system that uses a bank generalize from it, or only reproduce it? Existing benchmarks cannot tell, as they do not control how far a test question sits from the context. We answer both questions by comparing queries decision by decision, with a fast scorer distilled from human-calibrated LLM judges. Turned inward, the comparison diagnoses and repairs a bank. Fine-tuning on a cleaned BIRD-train bank beats a same-size random subset at every epoch (+2.6 points on average), and 92.4% of our removals had their SQL corrected by an independent expert audit, against 45.6% of audited entries. In-context examples that follow one convention beat those following the opposite one by 13.3 points, while a mix is barely better than none. Turned outward, the comparison generates test questions at a controlled distance from a bank, a pipeline we call CAT (Context-Aware Testing). On CAT-BIRD, for retrieval and fine-tuning alike, the benefit of a bank falls step by step with distance and is largely gone once about three quarters of a question's logic is new, and on CAT-Spider the benefit of retrieval likewise shrinks with distance.

### [34] [Cross-Linguistic Distinctive-Feature Constraints on Segmental Triphones: Evidence for Contrastive Dispersion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26837)
*Leonardo Araújo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Natural speech reflects articulatory and perceptual constraints, yet how these pressures shape consecutive segment transitions across languages remains underexplored. We analyze adjacent distinctive-feature distances in token-weighted segmental triphones across 17 Universal Dependencies corpora spanning nine language families, transcribed into IPA and mapped to 24 PanPhon features using Hamming and cosine metrics. Natural sequences exhibit an intermediate-distance mode (8-10 features under Hamming, except Vietnamese; 0.28-0.38 under cosine). Against an unrestricted within-word shuffled baseline, natural words reject the inventory-only null (W = 0, p < 10-4), showing higher expected distance, narrower dispersion, and lower joint triphone entropy in all 17 languages. Under a stricter within-word consonant-vowel template baseline, expected distance and dispersion are no longer separated, whereas joint entropy remains lower in 16 languages (p = 1.07x10-4). Entropy decomposition reveals higher mutual information between incoming and outgoing transitions in all 17 languages and all nine families (W = 0, p < 10-4), demonstrating sequential coupling beyond syllable-template alternation. Word-level mean-SD correlations and directional asymmetries do not replicate cross-linguistically.

### [35] [Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26841)
*Konstantinos Skianis,Aristidis Likas*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Weight-space programming is a frontier language model's recently reported ability to read and rewrite another network's weights without gradient descent. We investigate how examples can provide a weight update so that a weaker language model performs the task with nothing in the prompt, and study what it edits. Our experiments cover six tasks, four frontier editors and three families of weaker language models, without the editors being told anything about in-context learning (ICL). In most runs, the few-shot minus zero-shot residual is measured at the final prompt token, the ICL task vector, and write it into the weights, at its sparsest into near-silent MLP units keyed to the prompt format. Results reach the accuracy of ICL and of fine-tuning on the same examples, LoRA included, usually leaving perplexity untouched, with worse performance under changes of wording. We also qualify the comparison by counting unfinished runs, observing that one editor falls below fine-tuning; held only to the seen examples, without task pairs of their own, only the strongest editor has similar performance. Given a task and unlabelled inputs, that editor writes its own examples and does nearly as well on unseen items as with labels.

### [36] [How Long Will My Language Model Run? A Benchmark for Pre-Execution Runtime Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26875)
*Ashish Molakalapalli,Kangda Wei,Haonan Duan,Alex Carter,Ruihong Huang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Researchers submitting deep learning jobs to shared GPU clusters need runtime estimates to request time limits, choose hardware, and budget compute. Large language models (LLMs) offer a tempting shortcut: describe the job and ask. We introduce PreRun, a benchmark for predicting deep learning training and inference runtime from information available before execution. PreRun contains 801 training and 1,884 inference records of language and vision models collected on a GPU cluster, paired with workload configurations and explicitly defined timing targets. It also includes 64 text-generation configurations measured under standardized conditions, each in three separate program launches. We compare three LLMs (Qwen3.5-9B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Claude Opus 5.5) with regression baselines and evaluate analytical estimates on a supported forward-pass subset. On 16 held-out generation configurations, the open-weight LLMs underestimate latency by 90-99% on average without examples. Claude's zero-shot mean absolute error is 4.5 times that of a Random Forest fit on 32 configurations. Five labeled examples substantially reduce Claude's generation error, but their benefit varies across timing targets. We will open-source our data and evaluation pipeline upon acceptance.

### [37] [Isolating the Language Shell: A Content-Controlled Study of Multilingual Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27053)
*Hoejoon Kwon,Jinhee Jang,Byeonggeuk Lim,YoungBin Kim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multilingual reasoning distillation requires choosing the language in which teacher reasoning is presented, yet existing recipes often entangle linguistic form with differences in generation, translation, and filtering. We construct content-controlled supervision by rendering the same verified English trajectories into English, translated target-language, and language-mixed shells, and fine-tune two pretrained students in three target languages, evaluating them on multilingual mathematical reasoning at two difficulty levels. Even with the underlying reasoning content held fixed, we find that shell choice can change downstream accuracy, with effects varying across students, languages, and difficulty levels. Pre-training compatibility does not consistently track these outcomes, and even when our tests find no clear accuracy difference between shells, their output-language behavior can still differ substantially. These results suggest that the supervision shell is a distinct design choice in multilingual reasoning distillation.

### [38] [NightmareDiscourseBench: A Benchmark Dataset for Fictional Direct Discourse Identification Pipelines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27059)
*Claudia Carroll,Gabi Kirilloff,Dashiell Leigh*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: In this paper we introduce a new benchmark dataset, NightmareDiscourseBench, for testing NLP pipelines that identify forms of direct discourse in English-language fiction. We first review existing publicly available benchmarks (providing summary statistics and reviewing available metadata) for this task, identifying theoretical inconsistency and exclusive focus on speech as primary issues in this domain. We then overview our narrative theory-based framework for classifying and evaluating different forms of direct discourse, and finally describe NightmareDiscourseBench, a new benchmark test set of 12 text samples accompanied by metadata pertinent to the task of direct discourse identification.

### [39] [When Do LLM-Elicited Priors Help? A Controlled Audit of Language Models as Priors for Small-Sample Bayesian Regression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27075)
*Ran Zou,Yang Liu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked where to center the coefficients of a small-sample Bayesian regression, but the evidence is unclear: benchmarks are often built to match the prior and models may remember them. We audit this practice with one frontier and one flash-tier model, using hidden feature names, post-cutoff housing data and a pre-specified test that gives features the wrong descriptions. First, the models share their errors (correlation $0.92$--$0.99$ across draws, vendors and paraphrases): averaging $20$ draws is no more accurate than one, and treating draws as independent creates overconfidence. Much of this error comes from reporting each feature's effect alone, not with the others held fixed. Second, against the best classical prior, the LLM center helps clearly on one of four benchmarks (RMSE $-5.8\%$), marginally on two, and hurts mean RMSE on the fourth. Third, the LLM's stated uncertainty is unreliable; letting the data set the prior scale cuts the harm of a wrong center four-fold against a unit-variance prior. A pre-specified external test returned the verdict \textsc{partial}: on $18$ rule-selected problems the center helps on six and hurts on four, and a hard trust gate trusts a harmful prior while an evidence-weighted mixture is safer.

### [40] [How Far Does Lossless Re-tokenization Move an RLVR Update?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27083)
*Zhe Dong,Fang Qin*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Language models assign different probabilities to token sequences that decode to the same string. In reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR), a trainer that re-encodes sampled text may train on a different token sequence with the same reward. We ask how far this moves a training update, and whether the movement has a consistent direction. From one checkpoint, we compare updates on the same rollouts, canonical and with selected tokens split into two pieces, against an update on a different batch. On Qwen2.5-0.5B with three-digit addition, splitting about one token in 25 moves the update 0.556 times as far as replacing the batch. The ratio rises with the fraction split in four models and depends on which tokens are split; within a checkpoint, the displacements share a direction across batches. In a tabular model with one table per tokenization and a single sampled string, we prove that whenever two strings below an unsampled prefix differ in probability, only the zero full-gradient step agrees across tokenizations, however it is weighted. In an audit that decodes and re-encodes resampled rollouts, re-encoding touches up to 5.2% of rollouts but at most 0.08% of tokens, far below the split fractions we test. Training on fixed rollouts, the canonical arm finishes ahead in 14 of 18 pre-registered pairs; the interval for the mean accuracy difference includes zero over all pairs and excludes it only under the registered exclusion rule, which favours the canonical arm.

### [41] [Cross-Platform Production Signatures of State-Linked Information Operations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27137)
*Lin Tian,Marian-Andrei Rizoiu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: An information operation active on several platforms presents different names, personas, and topics on each. Its working routine is harder to change. We call this routine the operation's production signature: the regularities in when and how its accounts post, reply, and repost. We measure it from timestamps and coarse action types only, using no content, profile metadata, or network ties, as timing and action profiles for accounts and learned action-gap policies for populations. We then ask which parts of a signature carry over to another platform and which belong to a single operation. We train models on Twitter archives of four state-linked operations and apply them to Internet Research Agency (IRA) accounts on Reddit, with no Reddit training labels. They rank the IRA accounts at AUC 0.90-0.94. Content detectors on the same route fall from 0.98 within a platform to 0.81. Daily phase accounts for most of the transfer. Posting volume reverses direction between platforms, and action mix follows the role accounts hold on each platform. What transfers is not unique to the IRA: a second operation shares the same working-hours window, and action-gap policies separate every operation from organic accounts (AUC 0.96-1.0) without consistently ranking their own operation first. On 938 Telegram channels, groups that forward the same sources keep ordinary hours and pace but publish original posts in the same ten-minute windows more often than chance. This pattern is invisible when accounts are examined one at a time. Our results suggest that timing and action traces learned on one platform can help flag likely operations on another.

### [42] [CoPyro: Feeding Copy Proposals to Parallel Drafters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27217)
*Hong-Kai Zheng,Piji Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speculative decoding accelerates language generation by letting a target model verify several draft tokens in one forward pass. Earlier neural drafters such as EAGLE extend each candidate sequence one token at a time. Recent work has turned to parallel drafters such as DFlash, which predict a whole block at once. Another approach uses n-gram retrieval to find an earlier occurrence of the current context suffix and copy the tokens that followed it directly into the draft. We introduce CoPyro, which feeds these copied tokens into a parallel drafter in place of masks. The drafter learns from context which tokens to keep and which to revise as it predicts the block in its usual forward pass. Across eight benchmarks on Qwen3-4B, CoPyro improves overall acceptance length for all four parallel drafters tested, with gains of 2.19-5.08% when trained on 100K samples. With DFlash trained on 710K samples, overall gains range from 1.08% to 2.00% across the tested model sizes and temperatures. Code generation benefits most in both settings. On Qwen3-8B, processing the proposals adds an average of 0.24 ms per decoding round in Transformers.

### [43] [LongCat Recall Sparse Attention: Co-Designing Key Organization and Retrieval for Long-Context Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27233)
*Hao Zhang,Bin Xiao,Kefeng Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Retrieval-based sparse attention, exemplified by DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), reduces attention computation by selecting a small subset of key-value entries. However, selecting these entries can still require searching the entire visible history. For long sequences, retrieval becomes a major bottleneck, limiting the efficiency gains from sparse attention. To address this problem, we propose LongCat Recall Sparse Attention (LRSA), which combines fine-grained representatives with paged retrieval in an incrementally maintained index. LRSA partitions the sequence into time buckets that can be indexed independently as new keys arrive, without regrouping existing history. Within each bucket, it organizes indexing keys into capacity-balanced directional groups and packs a fixed number of complete groups into each page, retaining a separate center for every group. These centers provide fine-grained representatives for page selection, after which refinement scores members of the selected pages together with sink, sliding-window, and visible unindexed candidates to select the final Top-$K$ logical positions. To execute this retrieval process efficiently, we store members in reordered pages, fuse construction stages according to group size, and share storage for overlapping fixed candidates across queries during chunked prefill. These choices support regular member access while reducing kernel launches during construction and repeated candidate transfers. Moreover, we integrate LRSA into SGLang to maintain the index during inference, overlapping asynchronous index construction for new buckets with subsequent computation and reusing compatible bucket indices and member pages after a prefix match in the original key-value pool. With a 1024K-token context, LRSA accelerates key selection by 4.70$\times$ over DSA and combined selection and attention by 35.60$\times$ over full attention.

LRSA partitions the sequence into time buckets that can be indexed independently as new keys arrive, without regrouping existing history. Within each bucket, it organizes indexing keys into capacity-balanced directional groups and packs a fixed number of complete groups into each page, retaining a separate center for every group. These centers provide fine-grained representatives for page selection, after which refinement scores members of the selected pages together with sink, sliding-window, and visible unindexed candidates to select the final Top-$K$ logical positions. To execute this retrieval process efficiently, we store members in reordered pages, fuse construction stages according to group size, and share storage for overlapping fixed candidates across queries during chunked prefill. These choices support regular member access while reducing kernel launches during construction and repeated candidate transfers. Moreover, we integrate LRSA into SGLang to maintain the index during inference, overlapping asynchronous index construction for new buckets with subsequent computation and reusing compatible bucket indices and member pages after a prefix match in the original key-value pool. With a 1024K-token context, LRSA accelerates key selection by 4.70$\times$ over DSA and combined selection and attention by 35.60$\times$ over full attention.

</details>


### [44] [Do Companies Deliver on Their IPO Claims?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27273)
*Vidhyakshaya Kannan,Shiv Banafar,Michael Galarnyk,Sagnik Nandi,Soumeya Kannan,Shauray Arora,Abanoub Abdelmalak,Sudheer Chava*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Initial public offering (IPO) filings describe what a company does and what it intends to become. Yet whether individual forward-looking claims are subsequently realized is difficult to assess. We introduce Vision Follow-Through (VFT), a benchmark and agentic pipeline that separates claim extraction, category assignment, verifiability, and evidence-grounded follow-through assessment. \vftclaims{} contains 5,066 human-annotated claim spans from 50 IPO filings, while \vftverify{} adds verifiability tiers, follow-through outcomes, and cited later evidence for 1,000 claims. Across language models, classifying human-annotated claims is substantially easier than extracting claims from full filings. Extraction coverage also varies sharply by category, with Organizational/Culture claims recovered far less often than Market Opportunity claims. Follow-through assessment poses a separate challenge: model judgments diverge from human assessments in different ways rather than exhibiting a single consistent bias. These results show that reliable assessment of corporate follow-through requires both finding the relevant claims and grounding subsequent judgments in later evidence.

### [45] [Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27301)
*Md Shamim Ahmed,Lukas Galke Poech,Richard Röttger*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Clinical AI evaluations are vulnerable to observation bias embedded in routine medical documentation, which captures only what clinicians notice, test, and record rather than a complete clinical picture. As this evidence travels into publications and reference knowledge graphs, crucial distinctions disappear: unexamined symptoms blur with confirmed negatives, and chronological disease progression is lost. Surviving evidence can also enter both the benchmark query and the reference knowledge base, creating a self-referential loop where a patient is evaluated against clues derived from their own published case report. To quantify this bias, we tracked 6,503 clinical cases across six historical Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) releases (October 2021-June 2026) to identify when HPO first cited the publications describing them. This yielded a confirmatory cohort with an observable "source ingestion" event, where HPO cited a case's source publication as target-disease evidence. Diagnostic rankers depended heavily on these source publications: for our primary semantic ranker (Resnik), publication-weighted mean reciprocal rank rose from 0.26 before paper ingestion to 0.84 upon inclusion in HPO, but collapsed to 0.05 when source-linked assertions were counterfactually removed. Two additional rankers (IC-cosine and LIRICAL) reproduced this trajectory, and control experiments confirmed the diagnostic jump was driven by the patient's publication rather than background HPO growth. Clinical AI systems may therefore score well because their knowledge base contains evidence linked to the test case's source publication, rather than through generalization. Modern knowledge is not the problem; evaluation evidence must match the claim. Trustworthy benchmarks must separate patients, source-linked evidence, and time: historical tests should use only knowledge available at the intended decision time.

### [46] [Breaking the Long Horizon: Short-Horizon Process Supervision for Long-Form Generation in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27348)
*Heyang Xu,HanWen Hao,Qianren Mao,Zhuo Liu,Qili Zhang,Sheng Yang,Jianxin Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Long-form generation is increasingly important for agentic LLM systems, yet current reinforcement learning methods typically optimize an entire document with a single outcome-level reward. This delayed and coarse-grained supervision makes it difficult to localize errors and assign credit across semantically distinct parts of the output. To address this, we propose a short-horizon framework that reformulates long-form generation through semantic decomposition into segment-level decisions. Each segment is generated with prefix-conditioned context, allowing cross-segment coherence to be preserved while keeping supervision local. The generated segments are then scored with rubric-based rewards for adherence, coherence, and relevance, enabling explicit local supervision at the segment level. These local rewards are used to compute step-wise advantages, yielding localized policy updates. To isolate the effect of supervision granularity, we instantiate both outcome-level supervision and our short-horizon process reward method (SH-PRM) under the same GRPO framework. Across multiple LLMs and two long-form generation benchmarks, SH-PRM consistently outperforms outcome-level supervision and strong inference-time baselines under the same optimizer and comparable budgets. Further analyses suggest that these gains primarily arise from improved credit assignment. Overall, our results suggest that aligning supervision granularity with the semantic structure of long-form generation is an effective design principle for long-form LLM training.

### [47] [Silent Arbitration: How Large Language Models Resolve Co-Authoritative Conflicting Instructions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27444)
*Sihyeon Lee,Jiwoo Kum,Jihun Song,Chanwoo Kim,Chanjun Park*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models increasingly receive high-level instructions about roles, values, interests, and communication style. Such instructions can conflict even when a prompt assigns them equal authority and provides no priority rule. We study co-authoritative persona conflict, in which a single prompt jointly assigns two opposing personas. Across eight conflict types grounded in published source material and five LLMs, we measure conflict acknowledgment, resolution strategy, and directional stance. Models acknowledge incompatibility in 72% of direct checks but explicitly surface it in only 22% of task responses, revealing silent arbitration. Dominance accounts for 45% of dual-persona responses, and 35% of compromise-labeled responses retain directional lean. Prompt framing further changes the visible form of arbitration substantially more than ordinary paraphrase variation. These findings show that evaluating instruction following should assess whether models disclose conflicts, how they resolve them, and which persona their responses favor.

### [48] [Structurally Different, Functionally Persistent: Capability Regions Under Model Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27445)
*Jiwoo Kum,Chanwoo Kim,Doyun Kim,Seonghyeon Cho,Sihyeon Lee,Chanjun Park*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language model (LLM) capabilities have been associated with localized parameter regions, enabling targeted model editing and intervention. However, it remains unclear whether a region identified before model optimization remains an effective intervention target afterward. We evaluate the functional persistence and parameter overlap of coding capability regions across three instruction-tuned models under quantization, pruning, and LoRA-based adaptation. Although re-extracted regions exhibit substantial parameter reorganization, ablating the original region after optimization eliminates or nearly eliminates coding performance in almost all conditions, while magnitude-matched controls preserve performance. Partition analysis further shows that the shared subset of the original and re-extracted regions accounts for most of the observed ablation effect in the majority of conditions. These results demonstrate that parameter overlap and functional persistence are distinct: capability regions can remain causally effective intervention targets even when their parameter realization changes substantially.

### [49] [Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27494)
*Surapon Nonesung,Natapong Nitarach,Sittipong Sripaisarnmongkol,Kunat Pipatanakul,Warit Sirichotedumrong*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Typhoon OCR 1.5 focused on reading Thai documents. However, in real-world workflows, users often need to extract specific information or preserve the structure of an entire page for further processing. Typhoon OCR 2 handles both tasks in a single model, with prompt-driven extraction and structured full-page parsing. Full-page parsing covers Thai, English, and Chinese. We release compact 2B and 0.8B models adapted from open document parsers through supervised fine-tuning on curated Thai and public multilingual data, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task rewards and a rule penalizing unfinished responses. Among evaluated open models, Typhoon OCR 2 2B scores highest on Thai MDPBench (80.7 versus 68.9 for Typhoon OCR 1.5) and on ThaiOCRBench (59.91 versus 40.45), which covers recognition, extraction, and document understanding. The 2B model remains close to its base on English olmOCR-bench (84.7 versus 84.4) and on OmniDocBench, which evaluates English and Chinese together (90.97 versus 91.03). On MDPBench, GRPO reduces the mean share of pages with repetition loops for the 2B model from 3.2% to 0.7%, with a smaller and statistically uncertain score gain for the 0.8B model. We release the model weights, Python package, and evaluation suite.

### [50] [How Many Bytes Has a BPE Model Seen? Estimating Byte-Token Exposure in Pretraining from Corpus Statistics and Embedding Norms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27506)
*Liwei Zhang,ZhiMing Tong,Mochen Guan,Linzhe Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Byte-level BPE vocabularies retain 256 single-byte fallback tokens. When converting such a model into a pure byte-level model, these tokens provide the starting embeddings. How much training have they received? We estimate byte-token exposure in Qwen3.8 using two independent routes. First, we tokenize 540 MB of public corpora covering 40 domains and 33 languages, then combine per-domain token shares with assumed pretraining mixtures. Single-byte tokens account for 13 to 36% of tokens, mostly ASCII; genuine UTF-8 fallback bytes (0x80-0xFF) account for 0.15 to 0.27% under mainstream mixtures, or about 2 billion occurrences per trillion pretraining tokens. Fallback rates vary by four orders of magnitude across languages, reflecting how well each script is covered by the vocabulary. Second, we analyze embedding and output-matrix row norms for four open models, using untrained padding rows as a zero-exposure baseline and ordinary tokens with known frequencies for calibration. In all four models, the 13 bytes that cannot occur in valid UTF-8 remain at initialization, while every legal high byte lies in a high-frequency band. For Qwen3.8, the norm-based estimate agrees with the corpus estimate within a factor of four. The norm-frequency relation eventually folds, so inversion is useful only as a model-specific, order-of-magnitude estimate. No private data were used.

### [51] [Open CDLM: A Benchmark and Library for Continuous Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27536)
*Hao Jiang,Ruixi Chen,Jiayi Han,Yulei Sun,Yujian Chen,Gen Li,Brian.K Chen,Guang Cheng,Weijian Luo,Tianyang Hu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reliable comparisons of continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) require evaluating both model fit and the distribution of generated text. Two common practices leave this goal only partially addressed. Likelihood-based evaluation often reports a variational upper bound on discrete negative log-likelihood, whose slack can confound comparisons. Generated-sample-based evaluation commonly combines generative perplexity with within-sequence unigram entropy; both scores can remain favorable even when a sampler produces the same text on every draw. We introduce \textbf{Open CDLM}, a benchmark for evaluating CDLMs and their samplers, and describe the design of an accompanying open-source library to support reproducible comparisons. For likelihood-based evaluation, we clarify which comparisons of model fit are supported by reported perplexity bounds and how those conclusions depend on the evaluation procedure. For sample-based evaluation, we use \textit{Kernel Text Discrepancy} (\textbf{KTD}) to compare collections of generated and real texts, alongside diagnostics for diversity, validity, and coverage. In controlled OpenWebText experiments, replacing a collection of texts with copies of a single selected passage improves both conventional generation scores. MAUVE detects the resulting collapse, and its response to other perturbations depends on the text representation and the type of perturbation. This work marks the beginning of Open CDLM as an open-source project for CDLM research. We will maintain and extend the library over time and welcome contributions from the community.
