### [52] [Alliance Rupture and Repair in Simulating Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Dialogues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27544)
*Jian Chai,Yitian Yang,Siqi Liu,Yi-Chia Wang,Yi-Chieh Lee*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: In cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), routine work can strain the client-counselor working alliance, and the counselor must then notice the rupture, repair it, and adapt the work that follows. Existing CBT simulators model client resistance and follow structured treatment plans, but rarely track alliance state or allow counselors to repair ruptures over multiple turns and revise their plans accordingly. We present ALLY, a simulation framework that brings alliance rupture, repair, and replanning into ongoing CBT dialogue. Each client has a hidden alliance state that governs how openly the client engages. Like a real counselor, the counselor agent sees only the dialogue. It must notice when the client pulls back or pushes against the work, repair the rupture, and replan the rest of the session around what it has learned. Automatic evaluation shows that ALLY's counselors are closer to real CBT counselors than those of existing public synthetic datasets in strategy flow and emotional dynamics, and that ALLY is rated highest overall in counseling quality (CTRS) and interpersonal skill (FIS-T). An expert evaluation with 20 licensed therapists also finds the simulated ruptures plausible and the repairs and replanning largely appropriate.

### [53] [Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27652)
*Yunha Seo,Changhoon Kim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Machine unlearning is an approach to privacy protection: it aims to remove the influence of designated data while preserving the model's behavior on information that should be retained. While a growing body of work investigates this objective in autoregressive large language models, machine unlearning remains underexplored in diffusion language models (DLMs). DLMs generate text through iterative denoising, exposing partially masked states whose internal representations change throughout the generation process. This raises a DLM-specific question: can selective forgetting improve by identifying forget-data-associated features and adapting their suppression across denoising stages? We conduct a controlled investigation of this question in LLaDA-8B-Instruct. To evaluate the unlearning of knowledge plausibly encoded during pre-training, we use WMDP as our forget-domain benchmark. Using top-k sparse autoencoders and denoising-state replay, we compare static and stage-adaptive feature suppression. We find substantial shifts in forget-data-associated features across denoising stages, but tracking these dynamics alone does not reliably improve the forget-retain trade-off at the evaluated operating points. Together, our study provides an initial empirical foundation for developing and evaluating machine unlearning as a post-training privacy mechanism in DLMs.

### [54] [AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734)
*Minye Shao,Chenghao Xiao,Xingyue Zhao,Yang Long*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Foundation-model agents are increasingly extending beyond software engineering (SWE) into autonomous scientific research, where acquiring and integrating domain knowledge remains a critical challenge. Recent industrial advances have increasingly adopted knowledge graphs and ontology-based semantic layers to organize heterogeneous knowledge into reusable representations. We ask: Can autonomous agents construct ontologies that help them solve real tasks, and do they offer measurable benefits over alternative knowledge representations? Existing benchmarks evaluate ontology correctness or agent task success in isolation, leaving the value of autonomously acquired knowledge unresolved. We therefore introduce AutoOntologyBench, a task-grounded benchmark comprising 19,947 audited tasks grounded in 18 real-world knowledge sources across 7 domains, with source-native verification. Spanning Application, Repair, Organization, and Construction, AutoOntologyBench compares nine frontier-model agents under matched knowledge representations. Layered on retrieval, agent-built ontologies add 6.1 points of task success, yet trail an expert-derived reference by 13.0, identifying autonomous knowledge acquisition as the bottleneck to scalable scientific research. Code and resources are available at this https URL .

We therefore introduce AutoOntologyBench, a task-grounded benchmark comprising 19,947 audited tasks grounded in 18 real-world knowledge sources across 7 domains, with source-native verification. Spanning Application, Repair, Organization, and Construction, AutoOntologyBench compares nine frontier-model agents under matched knowledge representations. Layered on retrieval, agent-built ontologies add 6.1 points of task success, yet trail an expert-derived reference by 13.0, identifying autonomous knowledge acquisition as the bottleneck to scalable scientific research. Code and resources are available at this https URL .

</details>


### [55] [From Novel Combinations to Informative Absence: Structural permission, communicative opportunity, and form choice in language learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27762)
*Yanzhe Zhao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Language learners must infer which novel expressions are grammatically licensed and when continued absence is evidence against them. Our generative theory unites these capacities via counterfactual expression opportunities, decomposing utterance generation into structural permission, communicative opportunity, and form choice. First, shared predictive continuations recover structural permission for unseen word-construction pairings across 30 artificial grammars (mean AUC 0.945 after 120 sentences). Second, under hierarchical uncertainty, we derive a joint evidence law linking omissions to context diversity and within-context repetition, and an exact finite-sample context-refinement inequality. Thus, observing related expressions calibrates expected use to sharpen negative evidence, and higher expected use can drive steeper posterior declines for stronger-permission candidates (reversing initial order after six omissions in a fixed-rate example). Third, we prove that while raw counts confound semantic availability and form selection, scene-level opportunity observations identify both. Empirically, reanalyzing adult and child artificial-language experiments shows meaning-conditioned restriction; judgments of restricted combinations improve held-out production predictions across 399 participants (+0.036 nats/production). Naturalistic child-directed and child speech (11 families, six corpora) shows pervasive source-level usage clustering beyond lexical, number, and dependency-role controls, grounding hierarchical rate uncertainty. Finally, modeling causative judgments across five languages shows that structural compatibility and calibrated usage probabilities draw on distinct distributional, semantic, and discriminative cues. Together, these findings show how the organization and calibration of communicative opportunities govern the evidential value of linguistic absence.

### [56] [Enhancing Attention with Higher-Order Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27764)
*R. I. Cukier*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Current decoder large language models rely on a combination of attention, feed forward and residual layers. The attention used is autoregressive (AR) though this is not strictly correct, as we note. That motivates the introduction of other attention methods that, while also not strictly AR, do enhance the AR character. One is based on a decomposition of mutual information (MI) into a set of Conditional MIs (CMIs) that correlate key tokens with pairs of query tokens. A second, higher-order attention, introduces correlations between contiguous key and query tokens. A third introduces correlations between a set of key and query tokens and uses a Generalized Maximum Entropy Principle to obtain an attention expression spanning a sequence of tokens. All these methods may enhance the information content of the autoregressive probabilities that are used in inference/generation. Applications to contrastive decoding and a systematic analysis of autoregressive probabilities are presented.

### [57] [Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Zero-Shot Multilingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27807)
*Jakub Šm{í}d,Pavel Kr{á}l*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: While large language models (LLMs) have advanced natural language understanding, their ability to perform complex target-aspect-sentiment detection (TASD) -- a key task within aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) -- in zero-shot multilingual settings remains underexplored. Existing ABSA research predominantly focuses on English or relies on fine-tuned task-specific models, leaving a gap in understanding how open-weight LLMs handle compound sentiment triplet extraction across diverse language families and domains. We present a systematic evaluation of zero-shot multilingual TASD across 12 languages and three domains using seven instruction-tuned open-weight models -- ranging from 8B to 35B parameters across dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures -- under four prompting paradigms: monolithic, chain-of-thought, sequential, and sequential refine. Our results show that direct monolithic prompting achieves strong zero-shot performance, outperforming multi-step pipelines, while dense models consistently outperform sparse MoE architectures. Through fine-grained error taxonomy profiling and step-level pipeline tracking, we demonstrate that initial aspect term recall forms a hard bottleneck, whereas multi-step decomposition degrades extraction quality; iterative refinement only partially recovers this loss on larger models while inducing net-negative over-refinement on smaller architectures. Finally, generation volume analysis shows that multi-step strategies incur up to 2.38x token overhead without F1 gains, establishing monolithic prompting as the most effective and efficient paradigm for multilingual ABSA.

### [58] [MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27973)
*Chang Nie,Chaoyou Fu,Songlin Liu,Yiqing Hu,Caifeng Shan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

### [59] [Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26957)
*Zijia Cao,Hanqing Dou*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: 本文研究多智能体 LLM 流水线中"无支撑断言"（unsupported claim）在逐级传递过程中的漂移与失真现象，并提出一种"溯源感知"（provenance-aware）传输框架加以缓解。实验在五级顺序智能体流水线、FEVER 数据集中标注为 NOT ENOUGH INFO 的断言上进行，对比同质（同一模型）与异质（固定不同模型序列）两种配置下的"纯文本传输"基线与"带溯源信息传输"两种条件。基线结果显示断言在传递中语义漂移、不受支撑细节不断累积：同质条件第5级 Equivalent 仅 62.67%、UDA 0.311；异质条件第5级 Equivalent 仅 31.33%、UDA 0.590、语义漂移 0.194。引入溯源信息（支持状态、来源、证据、传递历史）后，同质条件 Equivalent 提升至 96.95%（语义漂移↓94.7%，UDA↓93.2%），异质条件 Equivalent 提升至 95.73%（语义漂移↓96.4%，UDA↓95.1%），且第五级溯源完整保留率达 99.93%。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 大语言模型常生成缺乏可靠证据支撑的内容（幻觉）；在多智能体系统中，断言被反复在智能体之间转述、改写、扩写，导致使用者与下游智能体难以区分"继承自早期智能体的内容"与"后期智能体新引入的内容"，可追溯性丧失使无支撑断言的识别与验证变得困难。已有工作多聚焦单模型幻觉检测（SelfCheckGPT、FActScore）、多智能体中的断言变更跟踪（Jamshidi 等）、智能体间信任评估（Epistemic Context Learning）与来源支持评估（AIS），但缺少对"断言内容"与"其支撑/来源元信息"分别跟踪的机制。因此本文动机在于：(1) 量化无支撑断言在五级多智能体流水线中如何演变；(2) 检验保留溯源元信息能否抑制这种演变；(3) 在同质与异质模型配置下对比纯文本传输与溯源感知传输的效果。

Method: 实验设计：数据集为 FEVER 中标注"NOT ENOUGH INFO"的固定断言集（证据既不支持也不反驳）；模型为五个开源权重模型（Gemma 3 4B、Granite 3.3 8B、Llama 3.1 8B、Mistral 7B Instruct、Qwen3 8B），本地推理以控制温度（0.7）、top-p（0.9）、最大输出 256 token、上下文 4096 token；每条断言经 5 级串行智能体（每级为独立推理调用、无持久对话记忆），每个断言用随机种子 0/26/42 重复，共四种情形：同质基线、异质基线、同质溯源感知、异质溯源感知（异质顺序固定为 Qwen→Gemma→Llama→Mistral→Granite）。基线仅传递上一级文本；溯源感知条件下每级接收结构化提示（断言、支持状态、来源、证据、传递历史）并返回 JSON 断言+溯源字段，全程不引入新证据、不做真实性验证。评价指标：(1) 五类双向 NLI 关系评估器（DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli，阈值经 145 条输出上 LLM 裁判+人工校正标定为 t_E=0.30、t_C=0.65），输出与原始断言 C_0 双向比较得到 Contradicted/Equivalent/Expanded/Contracted/Drifted-Lost；(2) UDA（输出中不受支撑事实单元占比，按句界、分号、换行、并列子句切分，NLI 蕴含概率≥0.50 视为被支撑）；(3) 语义漂移 SD（all-MiniLM-L6-v2 句向量余弦距离 1−cos）；(4) PPR（溯源完整保留率，需同时通过 5 项检查：合法 JSON 且断言文本非空、支持状态与所接收一致、来源一致、证据保留、谱系与传递计数与当前阶段匹配，忽略大小写/空格/证据顺序差异）。

Result: 基线：同质流水线 Equivalent 由 74.73% 降至 62.67%，Expanded 由 9.99% 升至 14.67%，Drifted/Lost 由 2.27% 升至 7.43%，Contradicted 约 10%–11.4%，SD 由 0.062 升至 0.104，UDA 由 0.207 升至 0.311。异质流水线退化更严重：Equivalent 由 93.53% 降至 31.33%，Expanded 升至 28.93%，Contradicted 升至 20.67%，Drifted/Lost 升至 12.33%，SD 升至 0.194，UDA 升至 0.590（Mistral 阶段出现跃升：UDA 0.466、Contradicted 19.73%）。溯源感知：同质条件全程稳定，Equivalent ≥96.95%，Expanded ≤0.51%，Contradicted ≤1.57%，SD ≤0.006，UDA ≤0.021，PPR 84.32%–93.57%；异质条件前三阶段 Equivalent 100%、PPR 100%/100%/99.67%，第四阶段 Mistral 为最弱点（Equivalent 95.80%、PPR 仅 64.60%），第五阶段 Granite Equivalent 95.73%、PPR 99.93%、SD 0.007、UDA 0.029。第五级对比：同质 Equivalent +34.28 个百分点，异质 +64.40 个百分点。

Conclusion: 溯源感知框架（将断言内容与其支持状态、来源、证据、传递历史分离并随断言一同传递）显著优于纯文本传输：它保持了原始命题语义，大幅减少不受支撑细节的扩写、矛盾与语义漂移，并使下游智能体与用户可获知断言的支撑依据与传播路径。框架本身不验证断言真伪、也不阻断断言传递，仅为审查提供依据，可用于研究摘要撰写等"上游智能体→报告生成智能体"的工作流。作者明确指出局限：结论仅适用于所测的同质配置与固定异质序列，异质序列中模型身份、流水线位置与前序变换相互纠缠，无法断定"异质性本身带来更大收益"；PPR 按阶段独立计算，不等价于全链路逐级无损保留；未来工作应探索替代模型顺序、分支流水线与反馈交互，并做组件级消融。

Abstract: This research examines how unsupported claims change as they move through multi-agent pipelines. It also examines whether preserving provenance can reduce these changes. We test both homogeneous and heterogeneous pipelines. Homogeneous pipelines use the same model across agents, while heterogeneous pipelines use different models. We compare the baseline with a provenance-aware framework. The framework passes each claim with its support status, source, evidence and transmission history. No new evidence is introduced during transmission. We measure changes in claim meaning, unsupported detail accretion, semantic drift, and provenance preservation. These metrics show whether the framework limits unsupported changes as claims pass between agents.

</details>


### [60] [Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27368)
*Dennis Gross,Jørn Eirik Betten,Helge Spieker*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: 本文针对并行协作式多智能体强化学习（CMARL）策略的安全性测试提出 DisQ（Disagreeing Q-values）测试用例选择方法。其核心信号是"Q 值差距"（Q-value gap）：协作智能体共享奖励训练，因此在同一状态下其最大 Q 值应大致一致；当各智能体最大 Q 值之间的总距离 D(s) 超过校准阈值 λ 时，即标记该状态为潜在失协调状态。DisQ 仅在初始状态做一次前向传播（无需与环境交互）即可筛掉不可能暴露失败的候选测试用例，从而降低 CMARL 昂贵的回合执行成本。该方法可与随机测试、遗传算法 SBST 等已有测试用例生成器组合。在 4 个基准环境（Simple Spread、Simple Speaker Listener、Coin Collector、Knight Wizard Zombies）、集中式与去中心化训练、2–6 个智能体的配置下，DisQ 在多数配置中显著降低所执行测试回合的平均奖励（最高 −36.2%）、显著富集失败回合（OR 1.19–6.80），且仅执行 11–39% 的回合预算。其优势有明确边界：局部奖励占比升高、初始配置对结果影响弱的环境、训练未收敛的策略、以及仅在中途出现差距的失败，都会削弱甚至消除收益。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 深度并行 CMARL 训练出的策略会产生违反"奖励未显式编码的隐式安全要求"的不安全行为（如智能体相撞），且难以解释；已有 CMARL 测试工作多聚焦对抗鲁棒性（扰动观测/动作，属安全威胁而非协作失败），而协作失败源自智能体自身学到的不协调。同时 CMARL 的联合状态/动作空间随智能体数指数增长，测试执行成本极高，因此需要能"免执行"地筛掉无望暴露失败的候选状态的测试用例选择方法。此外，单智能体 RL 的搜索式软件测试（SBST）方法虽可直接套用，但忽略了 CMARL 特有的信号：协作智能体对"共同未来"的期望是否一致。

Method: 1) 提出 Q 值差距度量：定义 Q_i^max(𝕆_i(s)) = max_a Q_i(𝕆_i(s), a)，总距离 D(s) = Σ_{i<j} |Q_i^max − Q_j^max|（所有智能体对的绝对差之和）；当 D(s) > λ（λ>0）即存在 Q 值差距。该指标可解释（数值小、直接反映"智能体对未来的期望互相矛盾"）、且只需单状态单次前向传播即可计算，无需执行系统。
2) 提出 DisQ 选择算法（Algorithm 1）：由任意测试用例生成器（TCG）产生候选初始状态 s → 计算各智能体 Q 值 → 计算 D(s) → 仅当 D(s) > λ 时才执行该回合，否则丢弃并重新生成；可作为"过滤器"叠加在随机测试与遗传算法 SBST 之上（遗传算法中对无差距个体赋予最差适应度 ∞）。
3) 阈值校准：先执行 n 次回合采集 D(s0)，取其 p 分位数作为 λ（默认 n=25、p=0.9；自助法验证 p=0.9、n=25 时相对误差 −3.9%±13.8%，高 p（0.99）在小校准预算下不可靠）。
4) 失败与评测：定义测试用例为初始状态，回合累计奖励 R(τ) 低于阈值 θ 即失败；鲁棒性用参数化 θ=μ−kσ（k=2），方法对比用非参数化 5% 分位数。指标为平均回合奖励 + 离散失败数/率/优势比（OR）；统计上以 25 次重复为单位，先 Kruskal–Wallis  omnibus，再 Mann–Whitney U 与 Vargha–Delaney A12，失败计数用 Fisher 精确检验，Holm–Bonferroni 校正，α=0.05。
5) 三个前提假设：(i) 每智能体有独立动作价值估计（DQN 类，排除 PPO/MAPPO/COMA/MADDPG）；(ii) 白盒可访问 Q 值（黑盒可考虑蒸馏替代值函数）；(iii) 初始配置显著影响回合结果（仅在 s0 评估）。

Result: RQ1（有效性）：在 8 个环境-训练配置中，去中心化下 Genetic DisQ 在 6/8 配置中显著降低平均奖励（A12≤0.04，OR 1.36–5.57），其中 5 个还优于原版 Genetic Testing；集中式下在 Speaker Listener 与 Simple Spread (2/4/5) 显著提升（奖励降低 8–36%，全部 p<0.001，OR 最高 6.80）。DisQ 方法仅执行 2,727–9,789 / 25,000 回合（中位 16%），如去中心化 Speaker Listener 中 4,444 回合找到 1,008 次失败（与随机测试 25,000 回合的 1,250 次相当）。反例：集中式 Coin Collector 各方法平均奖励上升但失败率显著上升（OR 1.62–3.55）；集中式 Simple Spread(3) Random DisQ 失败更少（OR=0.67）；Knight Wizard Zombies 几乎无差异（≤0.3%）。
RQ2（差距-严重度）：Simple Spread(2) 上选择分位数与平均奖励的 Spearman 相关在 DisQ 方法中强负相关（集中式 ρ=−0.95/−0.65，去中心化 ρ=−1.00/−0.82，均 p<0.05），原版方法无显著相关（|ρ|≤0.60）。说明 Q 值差距不仅可作通过/拒绝判据，还可按失败严重度排序与优先级化。
RQ3（边界）：(1) 局部奖励占比升高时 DisQ 优势衰减，超过 0.9 后实用上消失；(2) 初始协作影响小的环境（Knight Wizard Zombies，初始位置仅解释 0.4% 奖励方差 vs Simple Spread(2) 的 7.0%）无收益也无损害；(3) 需收敛的价值估计：去中心化 <8,000 步时原版 Genetic 优于 DisQ，集中化中期策略 Random DisQ 甚至选出更少失败（OR 低至 0.53），充分训练后 DisQ 恢复显著富集（OR=1.58, p<0.001）；(4) 失败回合分类：Knight Wizard Zombies 中 62.8–85.4% 的失败全程无差距，去中心化 Simple Spread(2) 中 82% 的失败有差距但仅 22% 在 s0 出现；执行中在线监控 D(s_t) 仅对去中心化策略有区分度（2.2 倍提升），集中化无（共享 Q 网络导致差距仅源于观测差异）。
RQ4（可解释性）：两个被选中的差距状态中，差距分别为 4.5 与 9.57（阈值 3.79、6.79），实际回合奖励 −83.07 与 −107，远低于智能体自身预测的 −40 与 −95，可直接用"智能体期望不一致"解释选择与失败。
有效性威胁：环境多样性有限；失败判定基于奖励阈值，无法严格区分"协调失败"与"单智能体表现差"（但奖励失败中协调事件的富集达 1.4–2.2 倍）；遗传基线个体仅编码初始位置，其余状态每次重置导致适应度为单样本估计，故遗传结果为下界；训练超参（γ、各智能体奖励归一化等）影响 Q 值尺度与选择行为。

Conclusion: DisQ 提供了一个轻量、可解释、免执行的 CMARL 测试用例选择机制：利用协作智能体共享奖励这一结构性质，从"各智能体最大 Q 值是否一致"中提取失协调信号，无需扰动系统、无需执行回合分析轨迹，即可与既有 SBST 生成器即插即用组合，在多数配置中以显著更小的执行预算暴露更严重的失败行为。论文同时明确了该信号的适用边界与失效条件——需要每智能体独立的动作价值估计（白盒）、需要已收敛的价值函数、要求初始配置对回合结果有实质影响，并且仅在初始状态评估因而无法覆盖中途才出现的失协调；作者指出在线监控 Q 值差距、MADDPG 式 critic 变体、策略梯度方法、回合制 MARL 及工业真实场景是后续方向。

Abstract: Deep parallel cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (CMARL)} trains multiple agents that all act at every time step to optimize a common objective. Like single-agent RL, CMARL can produce unsafe behaviors that violate implicit safety requirements not captured by the reward, and these behaviors are hard to explain. However, testing CMARL policies for safety has received less attention than the safety testing of single-agent RL policies. In this paper, we propose DisQ, a test case selection method that identifies failure-revealing states in value-based CMARL by exploiting a signal specific to trained Q-learning agents. The signal is the Q-value gap, an explainable metric that flags a state when the agents' estimates of the achievable return diverge by more than a calibrated threshold. DisQ selects such states for execution and skips those without a gap. Our experiments in four CMARL benchmark environments show that, in most of the evaluated configurations, DisQ improves failure detection over single-agent RL testing methods applied to CMARL, namely random testing and search-based testing with genetic algorithms. Our main contributions are the Q-value gap, an indicator of potential miscoordination computable from a single state without executing the system, and DisQ, a test case selection method that adapts existing single-agent testing methods to CMARL.

</details>


### [61] [Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27556)
*Wenqi Zhou,Leonardo Baldo,Edwin Kolbe,Manuel Arias Chao*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: 本文提出并试点部署了一个面向核电站反应堆监测的分层多智能体LLM助手（Reactor Monitoring Assistant），运行于瑞士Beznau核电站1号机组（1969年投运，全球在运最久反应堆）。该系统由一个编排代理（Orchestrator）拆解工程师问题并分派给六个只读访问单一数据源的专用子代理（NEA/ALA/OA/SSA/AEA/GEA/AMA/GMA），以自然语言"领域程序"（domain procedures）承载领域专家知识，输出严格限于咨询性质且每个结论均可溯源至原始记录。论文通过三个监测场景定性展示了跨ANIS/GARDEL监测数据、报警日志、变量定义、技术规格书与历史调查报告的取证与解读流程，并总结了向安全关键、受强监管的组织引入agentic AI的组织经验。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 1) 遗留核电厂的"数字孤岛"问题：五十年渐进现代化使监测系统（ANIS、2015年改造）、报警日志、变量目录、技术规格书与历史调查报告分存于彼此独立、从未为联合查询而设计的系统中，调查一次仪表异常需人工在SAP等系统中反复检索并依赖资深同事的经验。2) 知识传承压力：延寿运行使IAEA等机构关注的"经验保存与传递"成为持续议题。3) 现有研究的落地缺口：MindRAG、MAKG、Magentic-One、Farahani等的工业维护多智能体工作、RADIANT-LLM、Lee等的反应堆仿真、AROMA-GPT与Lim等的热流体实验设施，均停留在文档、仿真或实验环境；本文将LLM辅助推进到真实商用在运核电厂的调查工作流中。4) 安全关键环境对可溯源、访问受控、推理可复现、人类保留最终工程判断权的要求，叠加遗留电厂的复杂历史，使"协同编排式"工作流成为必要。

Method: （1）系统架构：编排代理负责解释请求、生成任务列表、分派与整合；六类专用代理各持单一来源的只读权限——NEA（反应堆监测知识、技术规格书、调查报告）、ALA（ANIS报警日志）、OA（组织架构与责任人）、SSA（ANIS与GARDEL数据同步性核对）、AEA/GEA（点名定义的语义检索）、AMA/GMA（执行监测程序与分析工具、检测异常）。（2）知识表示：领域程序以自然语言书写，描述特定监测任务下应检索与查验哪些信息，可由电厂工程师阅读、评审与随信息系统演进而修订。（3）软件实现：浏览器前端经REST API与后端交互；Agent runtime管理编排与子代理工作流；后端以数据库查询访问结构化数据、以向量库检索索引文档；语言模型经Azure OpenAI调用GPT-4o，使用瑞士境内Azure托管实例以满足数据保密要求；应用与数据存储本地部署，并用本地tracing平台记录执行轨迹与性能指标。（4）评估方式：三个定性案例——"你是谁"的范围自述、GARDEL异常检测查询（报告数据连续性、异常数量与区间，并对照ground-truth标签给出异常分数曲线）、以及一次表述模糊的ANIS"波动问题"调查（由编排代理结合领域程序定位上下文，联动AMA/AEA/NEA，比对历史调查报告并给出参考意见与后续待查项）；演示中注入合成故障，所考察的波动为厂商已确认、对运行无风险的已知现象。

Result: 展示了编排式多智能体架构在真实在运核电厂试点环境中的可运行性：编排代理可依据问题类型动态选择参与的代理（仅涉及责任归属的问题只需RMO，仪表异常则需多方协作），完成点名词义检索、跨ANIS/GARDEL监测数据分析与可视化、报警与历史报告取证，并把发现整合为带源引用的咨询性回复，支持"查看引用"以逐条核查证据；通过与历史调查报告的模式相似性比对，可为既有报告提供建设性反馈，同时明确"相似不等于因果"，因果判定仍需额外工程证据。系统证明了在保留证据链、程序可审阅、人工决策权的前提下，agentic辅助可以嵌入工程调查流程；同时给出组织层面经验：在以安全、可溯源、保守变更为核心的文化中引入生成式AI需谨慎的变更管理与评审机制。

Conclusion: 面向工业LLM应用必须围绕具体应用场景、信息来源与电厂人员既有流程来设计，而非仅靠模型能力。该Beznau案例表明：协调的代理编排能在保留证据可审查性的同时支持调查并给出后续行动建议（含相关文档与责任人指引），最终工程判断与运行决策仍由人员掌握。系统目前在Beznau以试点环境运行，下一步工作为：扩展到更多监测场景的系统化评估（检索准确性、分析正确性、对工程师的实际效用），考察代理协调的可靠性、对生成式解读的支持质量，以及随着电厂系统演进维护领域程序所需的工作量。

Abstract: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's question and hands the parts to specialized sub-agents, each with read-only access to one source. Domain expertise is written as natural-language procedures that plant engineers can read, review and revise. The system is strictly advisory, with every answer traced back to its sources. We also report organizational lessons from introducing agentic AI into a culture built on safety, traceability and conservative change. Beyond the technical architecture, the Beznau case study examines how an assistant can be introduced into a setting where evidence must be traceable, changes carefully reviewed, and operational decisions retained by plant personnel, paving the way for the responsible use of agentic AI in industrial plant monitoring.

</details>


### [62] [Communication-constrained multiagent risk estimation: a simulation benchmark for adult sore throat](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27468)
*Anas H. Alzahrani*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: Distributed predictive agents may need to approach a shared estimate under limited, unreliable communication. We evaluated classical symmetric pairwise gossip among five agents initialized from frozen calibrated predictions in a synthetic adult sore-throat benchmark. Ninety runs across three fixed generator families supplied 270,000 underlying test encounters, each observed through four missingness views. Complete, ring and star graphs were compared at eight interaction budgets and transaction failure probabilities of 0, 0.2 and 0.5. The coordination extension was designed after inspection of the predictive benchmark and is exploratory. Outcomes were disagreement around the conserved arithmetic mean and its exact decomposition of mean-agent Brier error. In the base view at eight attempted pairs and 0.2 failure, disagreement variance was 0.000109 for the complete graph, 0.000134 for the ring and 0.000175 for the star. The paired complete-minus-ring difference was -0.000024 (95% Monte Carlo interval -0.000030 to -0.000019). The centralized mean had base Brier 0.069781, compared with 0.069368 for Kumo alone. Agreement therefore does not establish superiority to the strongest individual predictor. Code, fixed probability inputs and results support replay without model refitting. The study quantifies finite-budget coordination under specified simulation assumptions; it proposes no new gossip algorithm and establishes no clinical accuracy or utility.

### [63] [Epistemic Social Learning: Latent Behavioral Structure under Endogenous Multi-Agent Interaction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27545)
*Jainendra Shukla,Dhruv Jaiswal,Divyanshi Beniwal,Kiriti Kanjilal*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: In multi-agent interaction, a learner's actions shape the observations from which it infers other agents' behavior. A behavioral model may predict these observations well yet support poor adaptation when opponents change. We introduce Epistemic Social Learning (ESL), which couples fast, interaction-specific Bayesian beliefs with slower online learning of population-shared behavioral prototypes. Belief-conditioned decisions influence subsequent observations and, in turn, the representations learned from them. Under explicit regularity and averaging assumptions, we provide a conditional stochastic-approximation characterization of these coupled dynamics. Across twelve synthetic $3\times3$ cooperative, coordination, and adversarial games, ESL achieves the lowest aggregate post-switch regret among the evaluated online latent-adaptation methods, including a switch-aware Bayesian filter. Additional experiments examine observation loss, noise, and asymmetric incentives. These findings illustrate how predictive fit can differ from decision-relevant adaptation under policy-dependent interaction.

### [64] [A Cognitive Agentic AI Framework for Interactive Process Analysis and Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27725)
*Trung Ngoc Trinha,Roman Tschentscher,Trong Dong Nguyen,Trung Thanh Nguyen,Anna Trubetskaya*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: Complex multivariable process analysis and optimization require coordinated access to simulation, structured data, machine learning (ML), optimization, and scientific literature, often across disconnected software tools. We present a Cognitive Agentic AI Framework (CAAF) that enables interactive, iterative process investigation through natural-language prompts within an established flowsheet. Following harness-engineering principles, CAAF assigns task interpretation, planning, knowledge synthesis, and context management to a large language model while delegating numerical calculations to specialized tools. Dedicated providers connect databases, scientific-document retrieval, ML-assisted Bayesian optimization (BO), and COCO process simulation. The framework is demonstrated on methyl acetate production. Guided by successive prompts, an engineer explored multivariable relationships, conducted 4,000 BO iterations to maximize carbon conversion yield (C-Yield) and minimize specific energy cost (C-SEC), refined operating bounds, and verified selected candidates through process simulation. Re-simulation of 16 candidates within the restricted domain showed close agreement with ML predictions, with a mean absolute C-Yield error of 0.0085 (0.85 percentage points). The highest BO-derived C-Yield, verified by COCO, was 0.921 versus approximately 0.81 in the initial dataset, an improvement of about 11 percentage points. CAAF also detects and reports non-converged simulations, excludes invalid outputs, and continues subsequent evaluations. The results demonstrate how human-guided agentic coordination can combine engineering tools for iterative analysis and optimization with rigorous simulation-based verification under a fixed process topology.

### [65] [Computing Weighted Set Covers with Heterogeneous Stochastic Oracles: Deadline-Constrained Token Complexity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26656)
*Jie Wang*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: 本文研究概率图灵机（PTM）如何调度多个"异构随机神谕"（HSO，如不同推理强度的 LLM）来求解带权集合覆盖（WSC），在给定截止期限与成功概率要求下最小化期望 token 成本。核心结果包括：全覆盖查询下用 LP 刻画每个可行成功概率的最小期望 token 成本，并证明最优策略只需在至多两条"预选批次序列"间随机化；两批次选择相对单批次全查的节省是非负次模函数，存在 FPTAS；精确优化 NP-硬但对正整数成本为伪多项式；部分覆盖查询下结合 primal-dual 局部对偶检验给出一轮成功率/成本界与自适应选择上下界，并构造出适应性带来线性 token 节省的实例。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 带权集合覆盖是 NP-难问题，加权贪心算法的对数最坏情形保证本质上已最优；作者的试点研究显示 LLM 在相当比例实例上能返回比加权贪心/反向删除更轻的覆盖，提示"AI 增强"的求解路线。但 LLM/智能体等查询响应型 AI 系统抽象为随机神谕后，其能力、响应分布、时延与 token 成本各不相同，必须回答：如何在截止期限 D 内、以成功率 η 达到带权阈值的完整覆盖，并同时控制期望 token 开销？同时需要不信任神谕自述质量、用可本地验证的方式给出近似保证。

Method: 建立 Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine（SOTM）模型：PTM 拥有有限个"调用机会"[k]，每个有截止时延 ℓ_i、成功概率 p_i、期望 token 成本 c_i；一轮内批次并发，后续轮次可基于先前响应自适应。全覆盖情形假设失败不变性（FICA）与失败-oblivious 选择，定义调度集合 ℬ 与 LP min{Σ w_B c(B) : Σ w_B P_B ≥ η, Σ w_B=1, w_B≥0}，证明任何策略可等价改写为"预先采样一条调度"的策略，且最优 LP 顶点至多两个正坐标。两批次节省函数 F(A)=(1−f_A)c_{[k]\A} 被证明非负且次模，用 (a,b) 枚举得到族 𝒜_{a,b}，配合按成本舍入的子集和动态规划给出 FPTAS。计算最优两批次选择由 Partition 归约证明 NP-硬，并给出 O(k^2) 截止对枚举 + 子集和 DP 的伪多项式算法。部分覆盖情形引入局部对偶认证条件 w(P) ≤ ρ Σ_{e∈N(P,R)} y_e，Lemma 1 保证保留部分覆盖的并为 certified ρ-cover；一轮选择用 r-折多重覆盖与贪心次模覆盖分析给出成功率下界 max{0,1−Σ q^{d_e(ζ)}} 与成本界 (1+ln(n r_1))⌈r_1/r_0⌉ OPT_η^risk；自适应情形用耦合 Bernoulli 变量给出成功概率下界与期望成本上/下界（Lemma 2、Theorem 5）；并用 Exact Cover by 3-Sets 的"all but one"构造展示残差引导查询的线性优势（Theorem 6）。

Result: (1) 试点研究：Opus 5.5 在 12 个缩减实例上，medium 推理下 33/36 次优于 WG、26/36 优于 RD；high 下 36/36 优于 WG、27/36 优于 RD；更大规模 24 次调用全部有效、20 次最优，中位时延 9.54 秒、24 次调用总花费 $0.646。(2) Proposition 1：一轮达到最大成功率 p* 的最小期望成本为 c_[k]；两轮为 min over feasible A of c_A + f_A c_{[k]\A}。(3) Theorem 1：策略可等价化为预采样调度；LP 精确给出各可行 η 的最小期望 token 成本；最优解只需在至多两条调度间随机化。(4) Theorem 2：F 非负且次模，存在 FPTAS，使 F(A) ≥ (1−ε)(c_[k] − c_2*)，即成本 ≤ c_2* + ε(c_[k] − c_2*)。(5) Theorem 3：2T-MaxSuccess 即使在统一截止、统一成功-成本比下也 NP-硬；当 c_i 为正整数时存在关于输入长度与 c_[k] 的伪多项式算法。(6) Theorem 4：一轮任意 ζ 的成功率 ≥ max{0, 1−Σ q^{d_e(ζ)}}，成本几乎必然 ≤ c(ζ)；贪心构造成本 ≤ (1+ln(n r_1))⌈r_1/r_0⌉ OPT_η^risk，常数 p、η 时为 O(log²n) 因子，当 1−η = n^{-Θ(1)} 时改进为 O(log n)；并证明 (1−ε)ln n 近似不可得（继承 Set Cover 硬度）。(7) Theorem 5：自适应选择的成功概率下界 η_U(u)=P[Bin(u,p̲)≥r_a]，成本上界 TOK_U(u)=c̄ΣP[Bin(t,p̲)<r_a] ≤ c̄ min{u, r_a/p̲}；普遍限制下期望成本 ≥ η r_b c̲/p̄，且需 η ≤ P[Bin(v,p̄)≥r_b]；同参数时两界相差 1/η 倍。(8) Theorem 6：构造实例中一轮成本 Σc_j，两轮成本 min{Σc_j, c_0+Σ p_j c_j}；当 c_j=c(n)、c_0=αc(n) 且 z>α+1 时比值为 z/(α+1)，即残差引导带来线性于 z 的 token 节省。

Conclusion: 本文给出了"截止期限约束下用异构随机神谕（LLM）求解带权集合覆盖"的系统化框架与理论刻画：以 LP 对偶提供不依赖神谕自述的可验证近似证书；全覆盖下刻画了成本—成功率前沿、给出两轮选择的 FPTAS 与精确优化的 NP-硬/伪多项式结果；部分覆盖下给出一轮保证、自适应上下界，并证明残差引导的跟进查询可获得线性 token 优势。结论强调：尽管存在经典最坏情形近似障碍，可验证响应与自适应选择仍能在具体实例上改进解质量。作者指出后续方向为在选择过程中学习未知的响应分布、token 成本与时延，以及在未缩减的真实大规模实例（尤其 OR-Library 铁路排班实例）上评测该认证选择方法，并强调任何分解都必须保持全局可行性与近似证书。

Abstract: We study computation in which a probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) uses AI systems, abstracted as heterogeneous stochastic oracles (HSOs), to solve Weighted Set Cover. A pilot study shows that an LLM can outperform weighted greedy. HSOs differ in capabilities, response distributions, latencies, and token costs. We study how the PTM selects HSOs to obtain, by a deadline and with a required success probability, a full cover satisfying a prescribed weight threshold, and we analyze expected token cost. For queries requesting full covers, assuming independent call successes and uninformative failures, we characterize by linear programming the minimum expected token cost for every feasible success probability. An optimal policy randomizes over at most two preselected sequences of oracle batches. Among policies attaining maximum success probability, the expected cost reduction of two-batch selection relative to querying all oracles in one batch is nonnegative and submodular. We construct an FPTAS for near-optimal cost reduction under heterogeneous response-time bounds. Computing an optimal two-batch selection is NP-hard but admits a pseudopolynomial algorithm for positive integral expected token costs. For partial-cover responses, the PTM combines returned sets across batches and turns. Once their union covers the universe, it verifies total weight directly or obtains a guarantee from LP-dual tests on retained partial covers. We give one-turn probability, token-cost, and hardness results and adaptive token-cost bounds under per-batch assumptions. A constructed instance shows that residual-guided querying can reduce expected token cost by a factor linear in the number of possible residual subproblems.

</details>


### [66] [Bayesian Optimal Stopping: Invincible Prophets and Achievable Philosophers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26829)
*Alireza AmaniHamedani,Ali Aouad,Senem Işık,Thomas Kesselheim,Amin Saberi*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study Bayesian optimal stopping: a hidden world $H$ is drawn from $K$ worlds according to a known prior and determines the joint distribution of $n$ observations. A decision-maker selects one observation irrevocably to maximize its value, learning about the world as observations arrive. We compare algorithms against the Bayes-optimal online policy (the philosopher) and the offline optimum (the prophet). Our results show that the philosopher is achievable in that we find a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation of the Bayes-optimal policy that runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(|\mathcal{I}|^{\log^* |\mathcal{I}| + 1/\varepsilon} \cdot (1/\varepsilon)^{1/\varepsilon^2})$, where $|\mathcal{I}|$ is the size of the input. By contrast, the prophet is invincible and no algorithm can obtain a competitive ratio that substantially exceeds the worst-case guarantees. When the observations are conditionally independent and identically distributed given $H$, the secretary's rule is $1/e$-competitive. We show that no algorithm can guarantee a competitive ratio better than $1/e + 1/\mathrm{poly}(K)$ and this bound is attainable. Our approximation scheme builds on a primal improvement subroutine connecting the two benchmarks. Given an $\alpha$-competitive algorithm against the prophet, we construct an algorithm with a strictly better approximation factor against the philosopher. We randomize between the baseline algorithm and a threshold algorithm based on dual martingales that exploit the Bayesian structure. Each improvement yields a tighter dual martingale, enabling repeated primal-dual updates. We approximate these martingales in polynomial time using importance-weighted Monte Carlo sampling. Dual martingales also establish our upper bound on the competitive ratio and may be useful for more general Bayesian online optimization problems.

### [67] [Revisiting Generalized Median Estimators: Exact Bitwise Computation and Gray Code Acceleration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26848)
*Robin Nunkesser*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Generalized median estimators evaluate the median of a symmetric kernel over all $M = \binom{n}{k}$ subsets of size $k$. Exhaustive evaluation was considered impractical even for $n = 29, k = 5$ ($M = 118,755$), prompting stochastic subsampling (Wilde and Grimshaw, 2013). We show that this barrier is computational, not combinatorial: storing all subsets requires $\Theta(kM)$ space, whereas stateful enumeration uses $\mathcal{O}(k)$ auxiliary state and retains only $M$ kernel values. We combine two exhaustive traversals with three-way Quickselect and a deterministic median-of-medians fallback, giving worst-case $\mathcal{O}(M)$ selection. Gosper's successor takes $\mathcal{O}(k)$ kernel work per subset for $n < w$; a Revolving Door Gray code changes one element out and one in, enabling $\mathcal{O}(1)$ kernel updates between recalibrations and $\mathcal{O}(M + kM/P)$ total time. We derive floating-point error bounds for the location ($h_1$) and mean-centered sample variance ($h_2$) kernels and their resulting median. For $n = 29, k = 5$, our ANSI C implementation evaluates all $118,755$ subsets in $0.74$ ms and $0.71$ ms, respectively. A direct C sweep places the crossover with partial lexicographic unranking at approximately $18,000$-$23,000$ subsets ($15\%$-$19\%$ of $M$), below the $32,160$-$45,420$ subsets required by Wilde and Grimshaw's sequential approximation at $\epsilon = 0.01$.

### [68] [Testable Testing: Distribution-Robust Property Testing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27033)
*Xi Chen,Renato Ferreira Pinto Jr.,Nathaniel Harms,Rocco A. Servedio*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We introduce a new model for property testing of Boolean functions, which we call distribution-robust testing. Distribution-robust testing is motivated by the hope of designing testers whose output can be trusted even when the underlying probability distribution does not satisfy the assumptions of the tester, while still being more efficient than distribution-free testers that make no assumptions at all. The purpose of this paper is to perform a broad initial exploration of this new model. In particular, we present a variety of general algorithmic techniques, which we apply to show that several well-studied properties admit distribution-robust testers that are significantly more efficient than their distribution-free counterparts. For example, we obtain constant-query distribution-robust testers for conjunctions, decision lists, and unions of intervals, all of which are known to require significantly more queries in the distribution-free model. These encouraging results suggest a range of questions for future work.

### [69] [Distribution-Robust Halfspace Testing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27062)
*Xi Chen,Renato Ferreira Pinto Jr.,Nathaniel Harms,Rocco A. Servedio*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Standard property testing algorithms are typically designed either for a specific input distribution (distribution-specific algorithms) or for an arbitrary unknown distribution (distribution-free algorithms). Halfspaces are an important example where distribution-specific testers can be extremely efficient, while distribution-free testers are expensive and essentially require learning. We introduce an intermediate type of algorithm, a distribution-robust halfspace tester, which must provide the same guarantees as a distribution-specific tester when the input distribution is the one specified, but must also provide a trustworthy answer under arbitrary distributions. This is achieved by allowing the tester to report that its input distribution is not what it expected (inspired by the recent testable learning framework of Rubinfeld and Vasilyan). We prove that distribution-robust testing of halfspaces under the standard Gaussian requires only $O(n^{2/3})$ queries, compared to the known $\widetilde \Omega(n)$ required for distribution-free testing. We also prove that sample-based distribution-robust testing of halfspaces is harder than sample-based testing under the standard Gaussian, requiring at least $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ samples compared to the known $\widetilde \Theta(\sqrt n)$ bound for the latter. In fact, we show that the latter $\widetilde \Theta(\sqrt n)$ bound becomes $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ when the covariance matrix is only mildly perturbed.

### [70] [Balanced Divide and Conquer for Rooted Maximum Agreement Forests](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27160)
*Feng Shi,Yexin Peng,Xin Zeng,Jingyi Liu,Qilong Feng,Jianxin Wang*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We develop a balanced divide-and-conquer framework for the maximum agreement forest problem on rooted binary phylogenetic tree--forest instances. The goal is a common subforest with the fewest components; budget $k$ bounds the increase relative to the input forest. We balance edges associated with an unknown optimum to obtain three subproblems with smaller budgets. Branching separates the inputs, while temporary marker leaves allow a global optimum to be recovered from independently computed optimal solutions. For any fixed $B>\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, the framework converts a tree--forest solver running in $O^*(B^k)$ time into one running in $O^*((\sqrt{\varphi B})^k)$ time. Starting from an $O^*(2.3391^k)$-time solver, two applications yield an $O^*(1.7743^{k^*})$-time fixed-parameter algorithm for two trees, where $k^*$ is the number of components in a maximum agreement forest minus one. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a fixed number of applications yields $O^*((\varphi+\varepsilon)^{k^*})$ time. Here $O^*$ suppresses polynomial factors, whose degree and constants may depend on $\varepsilon$.

### [71] [Tight Logarithmic Separations between LZ77 and LZRR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27213)
*Yuto Fujie*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: LZRR is a copy-based lossless compression method that produces a bidirectional macro scheme. It greedily parses a string from left to right. At each step, it can copy from an occurrence on either side of the current position, provided that the copy creates no cycle. Let $z$ and $z_{\mathrm{RR}}$ denote the sizes of the LZ77 and LZRR parsings, respectively. Under the original LZRR rule, we show that $z/z_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Theta(\log n)$ on a family of Fibonacci words and that $z_{\mathrm{RR}}/z=\Theta(\log n)$ on a family based on bit reversal, where $n$ is the string length. The Fibonacci separation holds under every tie-breaking rule. Both separations are asymptotically tight.

### [72] [Space-Efficient Text Indexing for Advanced Counting Queries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27432)
*Solon P. Pissis,Sharma V. Thankachan*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the classical problem of text indexing, the objective is to preprocess a text $T=T[1..n]$ over an integer alphabet $[0..\sigma)$ into a data structure that supports efficient pattern matching queries. Given a pattern $P=P[1..m]$, a reporting query lists the set $\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)$ of occurrences of $P$ in $T$, whereas a counting query returns $|\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)|$. Space-efficient suffix-tree variants use only $\mathcal{O}(n\log\sigma)$ bits and support reporting queries in $\mathcal{O}(m+|\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)|\cdot\log_{\sigma}^{\epsilon} n)$ time, where $\epsilon>0$ is an arbitrarily small constant, and counting queries in $\mathcal{O}(m)$ time. Notably, space-efficient indexes for more advanced counting queries have largely resisted achieving the same optimal (or near-optimal) query times when using less than $\Theta(n\log n)$ bits. We change this situation by proposing a general framework that supports advanced counting queries, denoted by $\phi_T(P)$, provided that $\phi_T$ satisfies two mild conditions: (1) $\phi_T(P)$ is an integer in $[0..|\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)|]$ that can be computed from $\mathsf{Occ}_T(P)$ via sorting; and (2) $\phi_T(Q)\geq\phi_T(P)$ for every prefix $Q$ of $P$. We show that our framework supports optimal $\mathcal{O}(m)$-time queries using $\mathcal{O}(n\log\sigma+n(\log\log n)^2)$ bits or near-optimal $\mathcal{O}(m\log_{\sigma}^{\epsilon} n)$-time queries using $\mathcal{O}(n\log\sigma)$ bits. As an example, our trade-offs improve upon the classical MAST index for counting non-overlapping occurrences [Apostolico and Preparata, Algorithmica, 1996; Brodal et al., ICALP 2002], which uses $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ bits and supports $\mathcal{O}(m)$-time queries, and the recent compact index for the same problem [Bals et al., ESA 2026], which uses $\mathcal{O}(n\log\sigma)$ bits and supports $\mathcal{O}(m\log n\log_{\sigma}^{\epsilon} n)$-time queries.

As an example, our trade-offs improve upon the classical MAST index for counting non-overlapping occurrences [Apostolico and Preparata, Algorithmica, 1996; Brodal et al., ICALP 2002], which uses $\mathcal{O}(n\log n)$ bits and supports $\mathcal{O}(m)$-time queries, and the recent compact index for the same problem [Bals et al., ESA 2026], which uses $\mathcal{O}(n\log\sigma)$ bits and supports $\mathcal{O}(m\log n\log_{\sigma}^{\epsilon} n)$-time queries.

</details>


### [73] [Shellsort with $O(n\log n)$ Average-Case Complexity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27671)
*Cheng Du,Zongqi Wan*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We show that Shellsort admits a fixed sequence of $O(\log n)$ gaps that sorts a uniform random permutation in $O(n\log n)$ expected comparisons. In fact, we give a distribution on decreasing gap sequences with this expected bound for every fixed input. We also give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, with high probability, constructs a sequence attaining the average-case bound.

### [74] [Kidney Exchange in Deterministic $O^*(4^{t+o(t)})$ Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27841)
*Binh T. Nguyen*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Kidney exchange admits a randomized $O^*(4^t)$ algorithm parameterized by the target number $t$ of transplants, but the best previous deterministic algorithm requires $O^*(6.855^t)$ time. We nearly close this gap by developing a deterministic $O^*(4^{t+o(t)})$ algorithm. Our approach uses Dynamic Representative Sets to execute the semi-feasible packing recurrence under a global cardinality budget of $2t$, exploiting a residual extension-budget invariant to avoid repeated static representative-family compression. To handle admissible cycles containing at least $t$ vertices, we establish a deterministic $O^*(4^{k+o(k)})$ algorithm for finding a shortest simple directed cycle of length at least $k$. Beyond feasibility, our framework supports additive optimization, yielding the same running-time bound for maximizing arc utility among packings with exactly $t$ transplants. Consequently, a packing that lexicographically maximizes the number of transplants and then additive utility can be computed deterministically in $O^*(4^{\tau+o(\tau)})$ time, where $\tau$ is the maximum achievable number of transplants.

### [75] [Geometrically Constrained Learning I: Agnostically Learning Adversarially Robust Classifiers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27852)
*Jane Lange,Cassandra Marcussen,Arsen Vasilyan*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study agnostic learning under the Gaussian distribution with guarantees on both classification error and robustness to adversarial perturbations. We say that a function has boundary profile $K \ge 1$ if, for all $r > 0$, the probability that a point lies within Euclidean distance $r$ of the classification boundary is at most $Kr$. We give an algorithm that takes a robustness radius parameter $r$ and learns a hypothesis with boundary volume $O(Kr)$ and classification error $\mathsf{opt}_K + \varepsilon$, where $\mathsf{opt}_K$ is the minimum classification error among functions with boundary profile at most $K$. For general $r$, $K$, and $\varepsilon$, the algorithm runs in time $d^{\widetilde{O}(K^2/\varepsilon^2 + K^4r^2/\varepsilon^4)}$. In particular, in the $Kr = O(\varepsilon)$ regime, the algorithm runs in time $d^{\widetilde{O}(K^2/\varepsilon^2)}$. Up to logarithmic factors in the exponent, this matches the statistical query lower bound for agnostically learning the $K$-profile class without recovering robustness. For natural geometric classes, including convex sets and Boolean combinations of halfspaces, this matches the corresponding surface-area-based running-time bound for non-robust agnostic learning via $L_1$ polynomial regression, up to logarithmic factors in the exponent. Our algorithm performs $L_1$ error minimization over polynomials, with an auxiliary coordinate roughly standing in for distance to the boundary. A convex constraint on the gradient of the polynomial, in this $(d+1)$-dimensional space, produces local certificates of the range of the polynomial on balls of radius $r$. Our algorithm finds a polynomial such that these certified ranges are small, then obtains a robust classifier via randomized rounding and partitioning of the domain.

### [76] [Linear-Size Spectral Sparsification by Sign Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27907)
*Trevor Vaughn*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Given an undirected graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and arbitrary positive weights, we construct a $(1\pm\varepsilon)$-spectral sparsifier with $O(n/\varepsilon^2)$ edges. For every $0<\varepsilon<1$, the algorithm succeeds with high probability and runs in time \[ O\!\left(n+\varepsilon^{-3}\bigl[m\log^2 n+n\log^3 n\,(\log\log n)^4\bigr]\right). \] In each phase we seek a reweighting that brings many edge weights to zero or twice their current value while keeping the relative change in every graph energy small. Reversing the weight changes preserves the error and exchanges deletion with doubling, so one choice deletes at least half the edges that reach an endpoint. We balance a smooth penalty for spectral error against a linear reward for alignment with independent random signs. Each step changes the free weights by a fixed fraction of their values at the start of the phase, with directions chosen from the estimated signs of the negative gradient. A weight stays fixed once it reaches an endpoint. We show that while few weights are fixed, the remaining edges admit a direction whose gain in reward exceeds its first-order spectral cost by a constant. The objective is bounded below, so this decrease forces a constant fraction of the weights to an endpoint. We repeat the partial coloring on the surviving edges, choosing the tolerances to keep the total relative error within $\varepsilon$.

### [77] [The Benefit of Migration in Throughput Maximization on Unrelated Machines and under Restricted Assignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27918)
*George Karakostas,Stavros G. Kolliopoulos*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In preemptive throughput maximization on parallel machines, jobs have release dates, due dates and weights, and the goal is to maximize the total weight of the jobs completed by their due dates. We study the benefit of migration, i.e., by what factor the optimal weight can increase when a preempted job is allowed to resume on a different machine. By a classic result of Kalyanasundaram and Pruhs, on identical machines the migratory optimum is at most $O(1)$ times the nonmigratory optimum. We give, for the first time, bounds for unrelated machines and for restricted assignment. We show that on unrelated machines, when every eligible machine can complete a job by itself, the migratory optimum is at most $O(\sqrt n)$ times the nonmigratory optimum, where $n$ is the number of jobs. Under restricted assignment it is at most $O(\log n)$ times the nonmigratory optimum. We provide instances which show that both bounds are best possible up to constant factors, even when the jobs have unit weights. Since our proofs are constructive, we obtain the first nontrivial approximation algorithms for migratory throughput maximization on unrelated machines and under restricted assignment.

### [78] [The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27934)
*Mayank Goswami,Vasilis Livanos,Pasin Manurangsi,Arturo Merino,GiBeom Park,Adarsh Srinivasan*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $\Theta(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid. A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

### [79] [One partition function call to rule them all: Efficiently computing the equilibrium landscape of multiple nucleic acid strands](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27945)
*Ahmed Shalaby,Damien Woods*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the nearest neighbour model of DNA/RNA binding, the partition function (PF) is a sum of Boltzmann-weighted free energies of the exponentially large set of secondary structures. Dirks et al. [SIAM review, 2007] gave a polynomial time PF algorithm for $O(1)$ strands, generalising McCaskill [Biopolymers, 1990] single-stranded case. Despite the intuition that PF may somehow encode the entire state space, thus far different approaches were required to solve various energy-landscape prediction problems. For example: finding the minimum free energy (MFE), structure(s) for $O(1)$ strands was open since 2007, and we recently solved [ICALP, 2025] via new techniques. We asked if there is a magnifiable PF algorithm [DNA31, 2025], which we answer here in the affirmative. We give an $O(N^3(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^2)$ space algorithm, for $c=O(1)$ strands of $N$ bases, the same overhead as Dirks et al. (non-magnifiable) algorithm. However, we show that magnification allows for efficient decoding of the entire landscape, concretely: a single call to the magnifiable PF efficiently solves and improves upon a large number of problems, giving: - MFE in $O(N^3(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^2)$ space; a considerable improvement over our $O(N^4(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^4)$ space result [ICALP 2025]. - The first polynomial time algorithm for the multi-stranded density of states problem, in time $O(N^3(c-1)!),O(N^2)$ space. - The first polynomial time algorithm outputting the entire list of energy levels occupied by at least one structure (in time $O(N^3(c-1)!),O(N^2)$ space), and the first algorithms for various energy landscape and counting problems. Our approach unifies the field of energy landscape prediction showing that a single, general, algorithmic framework neatly unifies a large collection of problems that practitioners care about, and required distinct techniques with worse time bounds.

### [80] [Cluster Editing in Subexponential Fixed-Parameter Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27956)
*Alexander Firbas,Manuel Sorge*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Cluster Editing asks whether at most $k$ edge additions and deletions turn a given $n$-vertex graph into a disjoint union of cliques. For more than a decade, the fastest algorithm for it was the golden-ratio algorithm of Böcker with running time $O(1.62^k+n^{O(1)})$. Cao and Chen had conjectured that the subexponential running time $2^{o(k)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$ is possible, but this contradicts the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). Recently, the breakthrough algorithms for 3-SAT of OpenAI and Anthropic refuted ETH itself. Our main result transfers running times from 3-SAT to Cluster Editing. If 3-SAT on formulas with $m$ clauses can be decided in time $T(m)$, then there is an algorithm that, given a graph with $n$ vertices and integers $k$ and $r$ with $2\le r\le k^{1/3}$, decides Cluster Editing in time $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}\cdot T(2^{O(r^2\log r)}\cdot k)\cdot n^{O(1)}$. Combined with the breakthrough algorithms for 3-SAT, this proves Cao and Chen's conjecture, as it solves Cluster Editing in time $2^{O(k\cdot(\log\log\log k)^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log\log k})}\cdot n^{O(1)}=2^{o(k)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$. The key ingredient is a sparsification theorem for Cluster Editing, the counterpart of the Sparsification Lemma for satisfiability: In time $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$, it reduces a given instance to $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}$ weighted instances with $O(rk)$ vertices and degree $O(r)$, each of which is equivalent to a 3-SAT formula with $2^{O(r^2\log r)}\cdot k$ clauses. Conversely, by a known reduction with linear blow-up, every saving in the exponent for Cluster Editing is, up to constant factors, a saving for 3-SAT.
